  • According to recent reports, the AirPods Max 2, which released in March, are already down to $449.99 from $549, saving you nearly $100 on Apple's premium over-ear headphones.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Amazon's early Black Friday sale is bringing some pretty significant discounts on Apple devices, including several of the company's latest releases. The biggest savings are on the M5 MacBook Air, with up to $249 off, though there are plenty of smaller deals worth considering, too, from the AirPods Pro 3 at $179.00 to the Apple Pencil Pro at $99. You'll also find discounts on iPads, the Mac mini, and everyday accessories like the Magic Keyboard, Magic Trackpad, and AirTags. With Apple raising prices across its Mac and iPad lineups in June, citing higher memory chip costs, these sales offer a good opportunity to upgrade without paying full price.

The AirPods Pro 3 are down to $179 from $249, saving you $70 on Apple's latest premium wireless earbuds. They offer improved active noise cancellation over the previous generation, along with redesigned foam-infused ear tips and a heart-rate sensor that tracks workouts without an Apple Watch. They also support Live Translation with a compatible iPhone and carry an IP57 rating for sweat and water resistance. PCMag’s review goes into more detail on how they perform.

According to recent reports, the AirPods Max 2, which released in March, are already down to $449.99 from $549, saving you nearly $100 on Apple's premium over-ear headphones. The biggest upgrade over the original model is the H2 chip, which Apple notes makes active noise cancellation up to 1.5 times more effective while introducing features like Adaptive Audio, Conversation Awareness, and Live Translation. For more on its performance, check out this PCMag review.

The Apple Watch Series 12 (GPS, 42mm) is down to $329 from $399, saving you $70. It covers everything you'd expect from a premium smartwatch, including fitness tracking, health monitoring, notifications, and the ability to take calls when your iPhone is nearby. PCMag gave it an "outstanding" rating in its review and also named it its Gift of the Year for 2026.

Sources indicate that if you'd prefer to occasionally leave your iPhone behind, the Apple Watch Series 12 (GPS + Cellular, 42mm) is $70 off, bringing its price down to $429 from $499. It has all the same features as the GPS model but adds cellular connectivity, allowing you to make calls, send messages, and stream music even when your phone isn't nearby (provided you have an active cellular blueprint).

For a more affordable option, the Apple Watch SE 3 (GPS, 40mm) is down to $199 from $249, saving you $50. It covers the essentials, including workout tracking, daily activity monitoring, and notifications, making it a practical choice if you don't need the Series 12's more advanced health features. Check out PCMag's review for a closer look at what you get for the price.

The Apple Watch SE 3 (GPS + Cellular, 40mm) is also $50 off, bringing its price down to $249 from $299. For an extra $50 over the GPS-only model, you get the convenience of making calls, sending messages, and staying connected without keeping your iPhone nearby, provided you have an active cellular strategy. It's worth considering if you regularly go for runs, head to the gym, or step out without your phone but still want to stay reachable.

Apple released the M5 MacBook Air in March with 512GB of base storage, double the previous generation's, along with a faster SSD and an N1 wireless chip that adds Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6. Right now, the 15-inch M5 MacBook Air (512GB) is down to $1,249.99 from $1,499. For a closer look at the M5 MacBook Air's performance and features, check out PCMag's review.

Industry observers note that if you prefer a more compact laptop but need extra storage, the 13-inch M5 MacBook Air with a 1TB SSD is down to $1,399.99 from $1,599, saving you $200. That's twice the storage of the base model, giving you more room for large files, photos, videos, and applications without having to rely as heavily on external drives or cloud storage. You still get the M5 chip, faster SSD performance, and Wi-Fi 7 support, all in a smaller, lighter design.

The M6 Mac mini is down to $949.99 from $1,099, saving you $149 on Apple's latest compact desktop. Its 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU can handle everything from everyday multitasking to photo editing and more demanding creative work, while the upgraded Neural Engine helps with AI-related tasks—Apple claims the M6 delivers substantial performance improvements over the earlier M4 model, particularly for graphics and AI workloads. For more on how it performs in everyday use, check out PCMag's review.

According to recent reports, the M4 iPad Air debuted in March, and the 13-inch model is already down to $949.99 from $1,049, saving you nearly $100. Its M4 chip can comfortably handle demanding tasks like photo editing, digital illustration, and multitasking, while the 13-inch Liquid Retina display gives you plenty of room to work across apps. You also get 256GB of storage for your files and creative projects. For more on what to expect, here's PCMag's review.

It has been revealed that if you need more storage for your creative projects, the 13-inch M4 iPad Air with 512GB is $100 off, bringing its price down to $1,149 from $1,249. That's double the storage of the 256GB model, giving you more room for large photo libraries, video projects, downloaded files, and apps without having to rely as heavily on cloud storage.

For those looking for something more powerful, the 11-inch iPad Pro with the M5 chip and 512GB of storage is down to $1,299.99 from $1,399, saving you nearly $100. Along with the faster processor, it offers an Ultra Retina XDR OLED display with ProMotion support for refresh rates up to 120Hz, making it particularly well-suited for creative work, video editing, and other demanding tasks.

The Apple Magic Keyboard with Numeric Keypad is down to $109 from $129, saving you $20 on a wireless keyboard designed primarily for Mac consumers. It pairs wirelessly over Bluetooth and can be recharged using USB-C. For a closer look at all that it has to offer, check out PCMag's review.

The Magic Trackpad is down to $130 from $149, taking $19 off an accessory that brings the Multi-Touch gestures and Force Touch pressure sensing of a MacBook trackpad to a desktop setup, across an edge-to-edge glass surface. It connects wirelessly over Bluetooth and has a rechargeable battery that lasts about a month between charges. You can read PCMag's full review to see how it stacks up.

The Apple Pencil Pro is down to $99 from $129, saving you $30 on Apple's most feature-rich stylus. It adds squeeze and barrel-roll gestures, haptic feedback, and Find My support to Apple's stylus lineup, and it pairs and charges magnetically along the side of a compatible iPad, including the M4 iPad Air featured above. For more on its strengths and limitations, check out PCMag's review.

In a recent development, the second-generation AirTag, released in January, keeps the original's size so existing holders still fit, while a newly introduced Ultra Wideband chip extends Precision Finding range by up to 50% and a redesigned speaker plays 50% louder. Right now, its four-pack is down to $79.99 from $99.99, which works out to $20 per tag, compared with $29 for a single AirTag. PCMag's review offers a more detailed look at how it holds up in everyday use.

According to recent reports, the Apple Magic Mouse is down to $59.99 from $79.99, saving you $20 on Apple's wireless mouse with a Multi-Touch surface that lets you swipe between pages and scroll through documents using simple finger gestures. It connects to your Mac over Bluetooth and has a rechargeable battery.

Yes, Apple participates in Black Friday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

Among the deals listed here, the M5 MacBook Air with 512 of storage has one of the larger discounts at $249 off, bringing its price down to $1,249.99, from $1499.

Recent findings suggest that for most people, the Apple Watch SE 3 at $199 is a good starting point, covering everyday fitness tracking, notifications, and essential health features without the higher price of the Series 12. If you want more advanced health monitoring and a more premium smartwatch experience, the Series 12 at $329 is worth considering.

#4623. Latest Update: PostgreSQL 19

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 23m • 📚 Deep Dive (4511 w)

Latest Update: PostgreSQL 19

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 23 min read (4511 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Postgresql

⏱️ ~23 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • PostgreSQL 19 contains many new features and enhancements, including:.
  • According to recent reports, newly introduced REPACK command that reclaims disk space and reorganizes table contents, which can improve query performance.
  • pg_plan_advice extension for controlling query planner decisions and pg_stash_advice extension that applies initiative advice automatically based on the query.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

PostgreSQL 19 contains many new features and enhancements, including:.

According to recent reports, newly introduced REPACK command that reclaims disk space and reorganizes table contents, which can improve query performance. REPACK (CONCURRENTLY) allows repacking without blocking reads and writes to the table.

pg_plan_advice extension for controlling query planner decisions and pg_stash_advice extension that applies initiative advice automatically based on the query.

Better performance in many areas, including automatic scaling of the number of I/O worker processes, quicker foreign-key checks, and further planning and execution optimizations.

Logical replication can now be enabled without a server restart when wal_level is set to replica.

Logical replication of sequence values.

Support for “read-your-writes” consistency on standbys via the new WAIT command.

Parallel autovacuum of table indexes and autovacuum prioritization through a upcoming scoring system.

The above items and other newly introduced features of PostgreSQL 19 are explained in more detail in the sections below.

Recent findings suggest that A dump/restore using pg_dumpall or use of pg_upgrade or logical replication is required for those wishing to migrate data from any previous release. See Section 18.6 for general information on migrating to upcoming major releases.

Version 19 contains a number of changes that may affect compatibility with previous releases. Observe the following incompatibilities:.

Add server variable password_expiration_warning_threshold to warn about password expiration (Gilles Darold, Nathan Bossart) §.

The default warning period is seven days.

Concern a warning after successful MD5 password authentication (Nathan Bossart) §.

According to recent reports, the warning can be disabled via server variable md5_password_warnings. MD5 passwords were marked as deprecated in PostgreSQL 18.

Remove RADIUS support (Thomas Munro) §.

PostgreSQL only supported RADIUS over UDP, which is unfixably insecure.

Force standard_conforming_strings to always be on in the database server (Tom Lane) §.

In a recent development, dumps created using pre-PostgreSQL 19 versions of pg_dump or pg_dumpall, and using standard_conforming_strings = off, will not properly load into PostgreSQL 19 and later servers. Users should create dumps using PostgreSQL 19 or later versions of these applications, or use standard_conforming_strings = on.

Client applications still support operations with servers having standard_conforming_strings = off, for compatibility with old servers. The server variable escape_string_warning has been removed as unnecessary.

Disallow carriage returns and line feeds in database, role, and tablespace names (Mahendra Singh Thalor) §.

pg_upgrade will also disallow upgrading of clusters that use such names. This was changed to avoid security problems.

Change the default index opclasses for inet and cidr data types from btree_gist to GiST (Tom Lane) § §.

In a recent development, the btree_gist inet/cidr opclasses are broken because they can exclude rows that should be returned. pg_upgrade will disallow upgrading of clusters with btree_gist inet/cidr indexes.

Disallow system columns from being used in COPY FROM ... WHERE (Tom Lane) §.

The values of such columns were not well-defined.

Change a json_array() call which returns no rows to return an empty JSON array (Richard Guo) §.

Cause transactions to pass their READ ONLY and DEFERRABLE status to postgres_fdw sessions (Etsuro Fujita) §.

This means READ ONLY transactions can no longer modify rows processed by postgres_fdw sessions.

Change default of max_locks_per_transaction from 64 to 128 (Heikki Linnakangas) §.

Lock size allocation has changed, so effectively settings must now be doubled to match their capacity in previous releases.

Remove server variable io_workers (Thomas Munro) §.

This has been replaced by four new variables; see Section E.1.3.1.2.

Change JIT to be disabled by default (Jelte Fennema-Nio) §.

Recent findings suggest that previously JIT was enabled by default, and activated based on optimizer costs, but this costing has been determined to be unreliable. This change requires sites that are doing many large analytical queries to manually enable JIT.

Change parallel vacuum leaders and workers to share the cost-based vacuum delay limit (Bharath Rupireddy) §.

Previously each worker process slept based only on the cost it incurred itself, so a parallel vacuum could consume several times the budget set by vacuum_cost_limit. With this change, VACUUM with parallel workers and cost-based delay enabled might run slower than in previous releases.

Rename column sync_error_count to sync_table_error_count in system view pg_stat_subscription_stats (Vignesh C) §.

This is necessary since sequence errors are now tracked separately.

Rename wait event type BUFFERPIN to BUFFER and rename wait event BufferPin to BufferCleanup (Andres Freund) §.

Remove wait event BufferContent and add more precise wait events BufferShared, BufferShareExclusive, and BufferExclusive (Andres Freund) §.

Change index access method handlers to use a static IndexAmRoutines structure, rather than dynamically allocated ones (Matthias van de Meent) §.

Remove optimizer hook get_relation_info_hook and add better-placed hook build_simple_rel_hook (Robert Haas) §.

Change psql's \crosstabview command to honor the \pset null setting (Chao Li) §.

Change full text search and pg_trgm to use the database's locale provider for character classification when parsing text (Jeff Davis) §.

Industry observers note that previously, characters were classified using libc, regardless of the locale provider. In databases with a locale provider other than libc (e.g., ICU, builtin) and where the locale configured through that locale provider behaves differently from the LC_CTYPE setting configured for the database, particularly a LC_CTYPE of C, the output of some full text search and pg_trgm functions could change. When upgrading such databases using pg_upgrade, it is recommended to reindex all indexes which use full text search and pg_trgm after the upgrade, and to recompute any stored tsvector values.

Change how fuzzystrmatch functions handle non-ASCII characters (Peter Eisentraut, Jeff Davis) § §.

According to recent reports, dmetaphone() and dmetaphone_alt() now upper-case their input using the database's default collation rather than always using libc, and soundex(), metaphone(), and difference() now treat only ASCII letters as letters. When upgrading with pg_upgrade, it is recommended to reindex any indexes that use these functions after the upgrade.

Remove MULE_INTERNAL encoding (Thomas Munro) §.

It has been revealed that this encoding was complex and rarely used. Databases using it will need to be dumped and restored with a different encoding.

Below you will find a detailed account of the changes between PostgreSQL 19 and the previous major release.

Allow NOT IN clauses to be converted to more efficient ANTI JOINs when NULLs are not present (Richard Guo) §.

Allow more LEFT JOINs to be converted to ANTI JOINs (Tender Wang, Richard Guo) §.

Allow use of Memoize for ANTI JOINs with unique inner sides (Richard Guo) §.

Allow some aggregate processing to be performed before joins (Richard Guo, Antonin Houska) § § §.

This can reduce the number of rows needed to be processed.

Improve hash join's handling of tuples with NULL join keys (Tom Lane) §.

Improve the planning of semijoins (Richard Guo) §.

Allow Append and MergeAppend to consider explicit incremental sorts (Richard Guo) §.

Convert IS [NOT] DISTINCT FROM NULL to IS [NOT] NULL during constant folding (Richard Guo) §.

The latter form is more easily optimized.

Simplify IS [NOT] DISTINCT FROM to equality/inequality operators when inputs are proven non-nullable (Richard Guo) §.

Perform earlier constant folding of var IS [NOT] NULL in the optimizer (Richard Guo) §.

This allows for later optimizations.

Simplify COALESCE() and ROW(...) IS [NOT] NULL to avoid evaluating unnecessary arguments (Richard Guo) § §.

Simplify IS [NOT] TRUE/FALSE/UNKNOWN to plain boolean expressions when the input is proven non-nullable (Richard Guo) §.

Speed up join selectivity computations for large optimizer statistics targets (Ilia Evdokimov, David Geier) §.

Add proper optimizer statistics for functions returning boolean values (Tom Lane) §.

Allow extended statistics on virtual generated columns (Yugo Nagata) §.

Allow function pg_restore_extended_stats() to restore optimizer extended statistics (Corey Huinker, Michael Paquier, Chao Li) § § § §.

Add function pg_clear_extended_stats() to remove extended statistics (Corey Huinker, Michael Paquier) §.

Adjust the optimizer to consider startup costs of partial paths (Robert Haas, Tomas Vondra) §.

Allow negative values of pg_aggregate.aggtransspace to indicate unbounded memory usage (Richard Guo) §.

This information is used by the optimizer in planning memory usage.

Improve performance of foreign key constraint checks (Junwang Zhao, Amit Langote, Chao Li) § §.

Improve asynchronous I/O read-ahead scheduling for large requests (Andres Freund) § § §.

Allow io_method method worker to automatically control needed background workers (Thomas Munro) §.

The new server variables are io_min_workers, io_max_workers, io_worker_idle_timeout, and io_worker_launch_interval.

Allow query table scans to mark pages as all-visible in the visibility map (Melanie Plageman) §.

According to recent reports, previously only VACUUM and COPY ... FREEZE could do this.

Allow autovacuum to use parallel autovacuum workers (Daniil Davydov) § §.

The maximum number of workers is controlled by server variable autovacuum_max_parallel_workers and per-table storage parameter autovacuum_parallel_workers.

Allow TID Range Scans to be parallelized (Cary Huang, David Rowley) §.

Improve COPY FROM performance for text and CSV input using SIMD CPU instructions (Nazir Bilal Yavuz, Shinya Kato) §.

Improve NOTIFY to only wake up backends that are listening to specified notifications (Joel Jacobson) §.

Previously most backends were woken by NOTIFY.

Change wal_compression equals on to use the best WAL compression method available (wenhui qiu) §.

Previously this always used pglz.

Change the default TOAST compression method from pglz to the more efficient lz4 (Euler Taveira) §.

This is done by changing the default for server variable default_toast_compression.

Improve performance of internal row deformation (David Rowley) §.

Improve performance of repeated UTF-8 case-folding operations (Andreas Karlsson) §.

Improve performance of hash index bulk-deletion and GIN index vacuuming using streaming reads (Xuneng Zhou) § §.

Improve sort performance using radix sort (John Naylor) §.

Improve timing performance measurements (Lukas Fittl, Andres Freund, David Geier) § §.

This benefits EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, TIMING) and pg_test_timing, and is controlled via server variable timing_clock_source.

Optimize plpgsql syntax SELECT simple-expression INTO var (Tom Lane) §.

Add system view pg_stat_lock and function pg_stat_get_lock() to report per-lock-type statistics (Bertrand Drouvot) §.

Add system view pg_stat_recovery to report recovery status (Xuneng Zhou, Shinya Kato) § §.

Add system view pg_stat_progress_repack to report the progress of REPACK, CLUSTER, and VACUUM FULL (Álvaro Herrera) §.

Add system view pg_stat_autovacuum_scores to report per-table autovacuum details (Sami Imseih) §.

Add vacuum initiation details to system view pg_stat_progress_vacuum (Shinya Kato) §.

The upcoming started_by column reports the initiator of the vacuum, and mode indicates its aggressiveness.

Add analyze initiation details to system view pg_stat_progress_analyze (Shinya Kato) §.

The latest started_by column reports the initiator of the analyze.

Add system view pg_dsm_registry_allocations to report dynamic shared memory details (Florents Tselai, Nathan Bossart) § §.

Add mem_exceeded_count column to system view pg_stat_replication_slots (Bertrand Drouvot) §.

This reports the number of times that logical_decoding_work_mem was exceeded.

Add slot synchronization skip information to pg_stat_replication_slots and pg_replication_slots (Shlok Kyal) § § §.

The latest columns are slotsync_skip_count, slotsync_last_skip, and slotsync_skip_reason.

Add update_deleted column to system view pg_stat_subscription_stats (Zhijie Hou) §.

Add sync_seq_error_count column to system view pg_stat_subscription_stats to report sequence synchronization errors (Vignesh C) § §.

Add stats_reset column to system views pg_stat_all_tables, pg_stat_all_indexes, and pg_statio_all_sequences (Bertrand Drouvot, Sami Imseih, Shihao Zhong) §.

It also appears in the sys and user view variants.

Add stats_reset column to system views pg_stat_user_functions and pg_stat_database_conflicts (Bertrand Drouvot, Shihao Zhong) § §.

Add location column to system views pg_available_extensions and pg_available_extension_versions to report the file system directory of extensions (Matheus Alcantara) §.

Add backup_type column to system view pg_stat_progress_basebackup to report the type of backup (Shinya Kato) §.

Possible values are full or incremental.

Add connecting value to system view column pg_stat_wal_receiver.status (Xuneng Zhou) §.

Add reporting of the bytes written to WAL for full page images (Shinya Kato) §.

This is accessible via system view pg_stat_wal and function pg_stat_get_backend_wal().

Add columns to system views pg_stats, pg_stats_ext, and pg_stats_ext_exprs (Corey Huinker) §.

Adds table OID and attribute number columns to pg_stats, and table OID and statistics object OID columns to the other two.

Add information about range type extended statistics to system view pg_stats_ext_exprs (Corey Huinker, Michael Paquier) §.

Allow log_min_messages log levels to be specified by process type (Euler Taveira) §.

Industry observers note that the newly introduced format is type:level. A value without a colon controls all process types, allowing backward compatibility.

Add server variable log_autoanalyze_min_duration to log long-running analyze operations by autovacuum operations (Shinya Kato) §.

Server variable log_autovacuum_min_duration now only controls logging of vacuum operations by autovacuum.

Enable server variable log_lock_waits by default (Laurenz Albe) §.

Add server variable debug_print_raw_parse to log raw parse trees (Chao Li) §.

This is also enabled when the server is started with debug level three and higher.

Make messages coming from remote servers appear in the server logs in the same format as local server messages (Vignesh C) §.

These include replication, postgres_fdw, and dblink servers.

Add reporting of WAL full-page write bytes to VACUUM and ANALYZE logging (Shinya Kato) §.

Add IO wait events for COPY FROM/TO on a pipe, file, or program (Nikolay Samokhvalov) §.

Add wait events for commit_delay and for WAL write and flush LSNs (Xuneng Zhou) § §.

Have pg_get_sequence_data() return the sequence page LSN (Vignesh C) §.

Add function pg_get_multixact_stats() to report multixact activity (Naga Appani) §.

Concern warnings when the wraparound of transaction IDs or multixacts is less than 100 million away (Nathan Bossart) §.

The previous warning was 40 million. Warnings are issued to clients and in the server log.

Add scoring system to control the order that tables are processed by autovacuum (Nathan Bossart) §.

The fresh server variables are autovacuum_freeze_score_weight, autovacuum_multixact_freeze_score_weight, autovacuum_vacuum_score_weight, autovacuum_vacuum_insert_score_weight, and autovacuum_analyze_score_weight.

Add server-side support for SNI (Server Name Indication) (Daniel Gustafsson, Jacob Champion) §.

Upcoming configuration file PGDATA/pg_hosts.conf specifies hostname/key pairs.

Allow OAuth validators to register custom pg_hba.conf authentication options (Jacob Champion, Zsolt Parragi) §.

Allow roles pg_read_all_data and pg_write_all_data to read/write large objects (Nitin Motiani, Nathan Bossart) §.

These roles are designed to allow non-super users to run pg_dump.

Allow background workers to be configured to terminate before database-level operations (Aya Iwata) §.

This allows database-level operations to complete more promptly since blocking background workers can now be terminated.

Allow server variables that represent lists to be emptied by setting the value to NULL (Tom Lane) §.

Patch GB18030 encoding from version 2000 to 2022 (Chao Li, Zheng Tao) §.

See the commit message for compatibility details.

Add WAIT command to allow standbys to wait for LSN values to be written, flushed, or replayed (Kartyshov Ivan, Alexander Korotkov, Xuneng Zhou) § §.

Improve function pg_sync_replication_slots() to wait for replication synchronization completion (Ajin Cherian, Zhijie Hou) §.

Previously, certain synchronization failures would not be reported.

Add server variable wal_sender_shutdown_timeout to limit replica synchronization waits during shutdown (Andrey Silitskiy, Hayato Kuroda) §.

By default, senders still wait forever for synchronization.

Industry observers note that this occurs during ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... [ADD|SET|REFRESH|DROP] PUBLICATION. Function pg_get_sequence_data() allows inspection of sequence synchronization.

Allow CREATE/ALTER PUBLICATION to publish all sequences (Vignesh C, Tomas Vondra) §.

This is enabled with the ALL SEQUENCES clause.

This is enabled with the REFRESH SEQUENCES clause.

Allow CREATE/ALTER PUBLICATION to exclude some tables (Vignesh C, Shlok Kyal) § § § §.

This is controlled with the EXCEPT clause, and is useful when specifying ALL TABLES.

Add CREATE/ALTER SUBSCRIPTION setting retain_dead_tuples to retain information needed for conflict detection (Zhijie Hou) § § §.

Also add setting max_retention_duration to limit retain_dead_tuples retention.

Allow CREATE SUBSCRIPTION to use postgres_fdw foreign data wrapper connection parameters (Jeff Davis) §.

Sources indicate that the connection parameters are referenced via CREATE SUBSCRIPTION ... SERVER.

When server variable wal_level is replica, allow automatic enablement of logical replication when needed (Masahiko Sawada) §.

Newly introduced server variable effective_wal_level, application pg_controldata, and function pg_control_checkpoint() report the effective WAL level.

Allow wal_receiver_timeout to be set per-subscription and user (Fujii Masao) § §.

Add optional pid parameter to pg_replication_origin_session_setup() to allow parallelization of SQL-level replication solutions (Doruk Yilmaz, Hayato Kuroda) §.

Allow GROUP BY to process target list subqueries that have expressions referencing non-subquery columns (Tom Lane) §.

Also fix a bug in how GROUPING() handles target list subquery aliases.

Allow window functions to ignore NULLs with the IGNORE NULLS/RESPECT NULLS clause (Oliver Ford, Tatsuo Ishii) §.

Supported window functions are lead(), lag(), first_value(), last_value(), and nth_value().

Add support for INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO SELECT ... RETURNING (Andreas Karlsson, Marko Tiikkaja, Viktor Holmberg) §.

This allows conflicting rows to be returned, and optionally locked with FOR UPDATE/SHARE.

Add REPACK command which replaces VACUUM FULL and CLUSTER (Antonin Houska) §.

The two former commands did similar things, but with confusing names, so unify them as REPACK. The old commands have been retained for compatibility.

Allow REPACK to rebuild tables without access-exclusive locking (Antonin Houska, Mihail Nikalayeu, Álvaro Herrera) § § §.

Recent findings suggest that this is enabled via the CONCURRENTLY option. Server variable max_repack_replication_slots was also added.

Allow GRANT/REVOKE to specify the effective role performing the privileges adjustment (Nathan Bossart, Tom Lane) §.

The GRANTED BY clause controls this.

Support forward references in FOREIGN KEY constraint clauses within CREATE SCHEMA (Jian He, Tom Lane) §.

Allow CHECKPOINT to accept a list of options (Christoph Berg) § § §.

Supported options are MODE and FLUSH_UNLOGGED.

Add CONNECTION clause to CREATE FOREIGN DATA WRAPPER to specify a function to be called for subscription connection parameters (Jeff Davis, Noriyoshi Shinoda) § §.

Add SUPPORT clause to CREATE AGGREGATE so extensions can specify support functions to optimize aggregate calls (Tom Lane) §.

Add memory usage and parallelism reporting to VACUUM (VERBOSE) and autovacuum logs (Tatsuya Kawata, Daniil Davydov) § §.

Allow ALTER TABLE ALTER CONSTRAINT ... [NOT] ENFORCED for CHECK constraints (Jian He) §.

Previously enforcement changes were only supported for foreign key constraints.

In a recent development, allow ALTER TABLE ... COLUMN SET EXPRESSION to succeed on virtual columns with CHECK constraints (Jian He) §.

This was previously prohibited.

Allow multiple headers lines to be skipped by COPY FROM (Shinya Kato, Fujii Masao) §.

Previously only a single header line could be skipped.

Allow COPY FROM to set invalid input values to NULL (Jian He, Kirill Reshke) §.

This is done using the COPY option ON_ERROR SET_NULL.

Allow COPY TO to output JSON format (Joe Conway, Jian He, Andrew Dunstan) § §.

JSON output can also be a single JSON array using the COPY option FORCE_ARRAY.

Allow COPY TO to process partitioned tables (Jian He, Ajin Cherian) § §.

Previously COPY (SELECT ...) had to be used to output partitioned tables. This also improves logical replication table synchronization.

Add EXPLAIN ANALYZE option IO to report asynchronous IO activity (Tomas Vondra) § § §.

Add reporting of WAL full-page write bytes to EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, WAL) output (Shinya Kato) §.

Add Memoize cache and lookup estimates to EXPLAIN output (Ilia Evdokimov, Lukas Fittl) §.

This can show why Memoize was chosen.

Add the 64-bit unsigned data type oid8 (Michael Paquier) §.

Sources indicate that add more jsonpath string methods (Florents Tselai, David E. Wheeler) §.

They are ltrim(), rtrim(), btrim(), lower(), upper(), initcap(), replace(), and split_part(). These are immutable like their non-JSON string variants.

Allow casts between bytea and uuid data types (Dagfinn Ilmari Mannsåker, Aleksander Alekseev) §.

Add ability to cast between database names and oids using regdatabase (Ian Lawrence Barwick) §.

Add functions tid_block() and tid_offset() to extract block numbers and offsets from tid values (Ayush Tiwari) §.

Add date, timestamp, and timestamptz versions of random(min, max) (Damien Clochard, Dean Rasheed) § §.

Allow encode() and decode() to process data in base64url and base32hex formats (Andrey Borodin, Aleksander Alekseev, Florents Tselai) § § §.

This format retains ordering, unlike base32.

It has been revealed that add functions to return a set of ranges resulting from range subtraction (Paul A. Jungwirth) §.

Industry observers note that the functions are range_minus_multi() and multirange_minus_multi(). This is useful to represent range subtraction results with gaps.

Add function error_on_null() to return the supplied parameter, or error on NULL input (Joel Jacobson) §.

Allow IS JSON to work on domains defined over supported base types (Jian He) §.

The supported base types are TEXT, JSON, JSONB, and BYTEA.

Add full text stemmers for Polish and Esperanto (Tom Lane) §.

The Dutch stemmer now uses a different algorithm, which changes the stems of many words; the previous algorithm is available via dutch_porter.

The English, French, German, Lithuanian, Norwegian, Spanish, Swedish, and Turkish stemmers have also been updated and produce different stems for some words.

Allow event triggers to be written using PL/Python (Euler Taveira, Dimitri Fontaine) §.

Add special libpq protocol parameters for compatibility testing (Jelte Fennema-Nio, Jacob Champion) §.

Otherwise known as protocol grease, which was active during the 19 beta period. These will no longer be sent as of the PostgreSQL 19 official release, but the parameter reservations will remain for potential use in the future.

Add libpq connection parameter oauth_ca_file to specify an alternate certificate authority when communicating with OAuth providers (Jonathan Gonzalez V., Jacob Champion) §.

This can also be set via the PGOAUTHCAFILE environment variable. The default is to use curl's built-in certificates.

Allow libpq environment variable PGOAUTHDEBUG to specify particular debug options (Zsolt Parragi, Jacob Champion) §.

The UNSAFE option still generates all debugging output.

Improve custom OAuth client flows (Jacob Champion) § §.

Previously, libpq reported only a generic error message during custom flow failures, and each flow implementation was required to calculate the issuer identifier independently. Add a newly introduced authdata hook type PQAUTHDATA_OAUTH_BEARER_TOKEN_V2 that precomputes the issuer ID and lets hooks provide error details.

Add libpq function PQgetThreadLock() to retrieve the current locking callback (Jacob Champion) §.

Allow the search path to appear in the psql prompt via %S (Florents Tselai) §.

This works when psql is connected to PostgreSQL 18 or later.

Allow the hot standby status to appear in the psql prompt via %i (Jim Jones) §.

Modify psql backslash commands to show comments for publications, subscriptions, and extended statistics (Fujii Masao, Jim Jones) §.

The modified commands are \dRp+, \dRs+, and \dX+.

Allow control over how booleans are displayed in psql (David G. Johnston) §.

The \pset variables are display_true and display_false.

Allow psql to more accurately determine if the pager is needed (Erik Wienhold) §.

Add or improve psql tab completion (Yamaguchi Atsuo, Yugo Nagata, Haruna Miwa, Xuneng Zhou, Dagfinn Ilmari Mannsåker, Fujii Masao, Álvaro Herrera, Jian He, Tatsuya Kawata, Ian Lawrence Barwick, Vasuki M) § § § § § § § § § § § § § §.

Allow pg_dump to include restorable extended statistics (Corey Huinker) §.

Change vacuumdb's --analyze-only and --analyze-in-stages options to analyze partitioned tables when no targets are specified (Laurenz Albe, Mircea Cadariu, Chao Li) § §.

Sources indicate that previously it skipped partitioned tables. This now matches the behavior of ANALYZE.

Allow vacuumdb to report its commands without running them using option --dry-run (Corey Huinker) §.

Allow pg_verifybackup to read WAL files stored in tar archives (Amul Sul) §.

Add option --wal-path as an alias for the existing and deprecated --wal-directory option.

Allow pg_waldump to read WAL files stored in tar archives (Amul Sul) §.

Improve performance of pg_upgrade copying large object metadata (Nathan Bossart) § § § §.

Various methods are used, depending on the PostgreSQL version of the old cluster.

Allow pg_upgrade to process non-default tablespaces stored in the PGDATA directory (Nathan Bossart) §.

Previously such tablespaces generated an error.

Add pgbench option --continue-on-error to continue after SQL errors (Rintaro Ikeda, Yugo Nagata, Fujii Masao) §.

Improve the usability of pg_test_timing (Hannu Krosing, Tom Lane) § §.

Report nanoseconds instead of microseconds. In addition to histogram output, output a second table that reports exact timings, with an optional cutoff set by --cutoff.

Previously this generated an error.

Restore support for AIX (Aditya Kamath, Srirama Kucherlapati, Peter Eisentraut) § §.

This uses gcc and only supports 64-bit builds.

Change Solaris to use unnamed POSIX semaphores (Tom Lane) §.

Previously it used System V semaphores.

Require Visual Studio 2019 or later (Peter Eisentraut) §.

Allow MSVC to create PL/Python using the Python Limited API (Bryan Green) §.

Allow building on AArch64 using MSVC (Niyas Sait, Greg Burd, Dave Cramer) §.

Allow execution stack backtraces on Windows using DbgHelp (Bryan Green) §.

Change the supported C language version to C11 (Peter Eisentraut) § §.

Use standard C23 and C++ attributes if available (Peter Eisentraut) §.

Use AVX2 CPU instructions for calculating page checksums (Matthew Sterrett, Andrew Kim) §.

Use ARM Crypto Extension to Compute CRC32C (John Naylor) §.

Change hex_encode() and hex_decode() to use SIMD CPU instructions (Nathan Bossart, Chiranmoy Bhattacharya) §.

Require Meson version 0.57.2 or later (Peter Eisentraut) §.

Add Meson option to build both shared and static libraries, or only shared (Peter Eisentraut) §.

Upgrade Unicode data to version 17.0.0 (Peter Eisentraut) §.

Add hooks planner_setup_hook, planner_shutdown_hook, joinrel_setup_hook, and join_path_setup_hook (Robert Haas) § §.

Allow extensions to replace set-returning functions in the FROM clause with SQL queries (Paul A. Jungwirth) §.

Make multixact members 64-bit (Maxim Orlov) §.

Change function prototypes to use uint* instead of bit* typedefs (Nathan Bossart) §.

Allow OAuth validators to supply failure details (Jacob Champion) §.

This is done by setting the ValidatorModuleResult structure member error_detail.

Add simplified and improved shared memory registration function ShmemRequestStruct() (Heikki Linnakangas, Ashutosh Bapat) §.

Functions ShmemInitStruct() and ShmemInitHash() remain for backward compatibility.

Add server variable debug_exec_backend to report how parameters are passed to new backends (Daniel Gustafsson) §.

Add documentation section about temporal tables (Paul A. Jungwirth) §.

Document the environment variables that control the regression tests (Michael Paquier) §.

Update documented systemd example to include a restart setting (Andrew Jackson) §.

Add pg_plan_advice module to stabilize and control planner decisions (Robert Haas) § §.

Add extension pg_stash_advice to allow per-query-id advice to be specified (Robert Haas, Lukas Fittl) § §.

Show sizes of FETCH queries as constants in pg_stat_statements (Sami Imseih) §.

Fetches of different sizes will now be grouped together in pg_stat_statements output.

Add generic and custom blueprint counts to pg_stat_statements (Sami Imseih) §.

Refactor pg_buffercache reporting of shared memory mapping (Bertrand Drouvot) §.

New function pg_buffercache_os_pages() and system view pg_buffercache_os_pages allow reporting of shared memory mapping; the function optionally includes NUMA details. Function pg_buffercache_numa_pages() remains for backward compatibility.

Add functions to pg_buffercache to mark buffers as dirty (Nazir Bilal Yavuz) §.

The functions are pg_buffercache_mark_dirty(), pg_buffercache_mark_dirty_relation(), and pg_buffercache_mark_dirty_all().

Allow pushdown of array comparisons in prepared statements to postgres_fdw foreign servers (Alexander Pyhalov) §.

Allow the retrieval of statistics from foreign data wrapper servers (Corey Huinker, Etsuro Fujita) § §.

This is enabled for postgres_fdw by using the option import_stats. The default is for ANALYZE to retrieve rows from the remote server to locally generate statistics.

Allow file_fdw to read files or program output that uses multi-line headers (Shinya Kato) §.

Add server variable auto_explain.log_io to add IO reporting to auto_explain (Tomas Vondra) §.

Allow auto_explain to add extension-specific EXPLAIN options via server variable auto_explain.log_extension_options (Robert Haas) §.

Change btree_gin to support all btree-supported cross-type comparisons (Tom Lane) § §.

Improve performance of bloom indexes by using streaming reads (Xuneng Zhou) § §.

Improve performance of pgstattuple by using streaming reads (Xuneng Zhou) § §.

Modify oid2name --extended to report the relation file path (David Bidoc) §.

#4621. Tech Report: 25 Years Later, Steven Spielberg’s Sci-Fi Classic Officially Returns in 4K

Tech Report: 25 Years Later, Steven Spielberg’s Sci-Fi Classic Officially Returns in 4K

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (399 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Collider

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Steven Spielberg made his grand return to science fiction this year with Disclosure Day.
  • Artificial Intelligence was a collaboration between the unusual pairing of Spielberg and Stanley Kubrick.
  • Artificial Intelligence will soon be available in a handsome newly introduced SteelBook edition for its 25th anniversary.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Steven Spielberg made his grand return to science fiction this year with Disclosure Day. The director has a widely varied filmography, but sci-fi is the genre he most frequently returns to. Now, for its 25th anniversary, one of his most underappreciated science fiction films is coming home in a new 4K Blu-ray SteelBook edition.

A.I. Artificial Intelligence was a collaboration between the unusual pairing of Spielberg and Stanley Kubrick. The film began life as "Supertoys Last All Summer Long," a short story by Brian Aldiss; Kubrick acquired the rights to the story in the 1970s and commissioned a number of scripts for the film; however, it became one of the director's many unfinished projects when he died in 1999. Kubrick had previously discussed handing the project over to Spielberg, as he believed it suited the E.T. director's sensibilities; Spielberg then took over the project after Kubrick's death.

And now, A.I. Artificial Intelligence will soon be available in a handsome newly introduced SteelBook edition for its 25th anniversary. The two-disc set will include the film on both standard-definition Blu-ray and Ultra HD 4K. It will also include a number of special features, including featurettes on the movie's creation, action, design, lighting, special effects, music and sound, and its robotic creations; a message from Spielberg on the responsibilities associated with creating artificial intelligence; and the film's theatrical trailers. It will be available on December 15.

It has been revealed that set in the 22nd century, when global warming has decreased the human population and devastated coastal areas, humanity has turned to robots, known as mechas, for service and companionship. Monica (Frances O'Connor) and Henry (Sam Robards) are a wealthy couple whose only son, Martin (Jake Thomas), is in suspended animation while a cure is sought for the rare disease he suffers from. To assuage their loneliness, they acquire David (Haley Joel Osment), a robotic prototype child who they soon come to care for. However, when Martin's disease is cured, he comes to resent David; soon, Monica abandons David in the wilderness, where he seeks out a way to become human and regain the love of his "mother" with the help of his robotic bear, Teddy (Jack Angel) and robotic prostitute Gigolo Joe (Jude Law).

A.I. Artificial Intelligence will be available in a limited edition 4K Blu-ray SteelBook on December 15. Stay tuned to Collider for future updates.

#4619. 10 Indicates Like 'MobLand' You Should Watch Next

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1287 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

10 Indicates Like 'MobLand' You Should Watch Next

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1287 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that crime dramas often attract massive stars, and MobLand is no exception.
  • According to recent reports, while families are complicated in even the best of circumstances, that's especially true of the Family.
  • Recent findings suggest that theo James plays army officer Eddie Horniman (a name mentioned as often as possible), heir to the Horniman estate (there it is again) who, upon the death of his father, is named the Duke of Halstead.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that crime dramas often attract massive stars, and MobLand is no exception. The Paramount+ series stars Tom Hardy as mob fixer Harry Da Souza, with Pierce Brosnan and Paddy Considine in supporting roles and Helen Mirren having a ball as the thoroughly evil matriarch of the Harrigan crime family.

According to recent reports, while families are complicated in even the best of circumstances, that's especially true of the Family. After you've watched the recently released second season of MobLand, try one of these other highlights mixing crime and family (or Family) drama.

Recent findings suggest that theo James plays army officer Eddie Horniman (a name mentioned as often as possible), heir to the Horniman estate (there it is again) who, upon the death of his father, is named the Duke of Halstead. He learns that his dad was tied to various criminal enterprises, and that his scouse brother is millions of pounds in debt to a drug dealer. What else is the dapper, military-trained Duke to do but learn to navigate the violent underworld while looking cool? You won't be surprised to learn that this British crime drama comes from creator/writer/producer Guy Ritchie, who also has a hand in MobLand. Stream The Gentlemen on Netflix.

It has been revealed that another series from Taylor Sheridan (the Yellowstone guy), this pandemic-era hit stars Jeremy Renner as Mike McLusky, head of a family that’s been keeping the peace, through means fair and foul, in the title's company town for decades. The "business" of the corrupt burg happens to be incarceration, and the McLuskys thrive when business is up, even if Mike has slightly different ideas about how to run things. The show deals broadly with systemic racism and inequality in the prison system, but mostly it's a modern-day western about bringing justice to a corrupt town. It will conclude with a fifth season, streaming in 2027. Stream Mayor of Kingstown on Paramount+.

It has been revealed that A consistently compelling combination of smart plotting and lurid sex and violence, Banshee stars Antony Starr as Sheriff Lucas Hood...kinda: He's actually a man recently released from prison who takes over that identity when the new sheriff in the small town of Banshee is killed before anyone really has a chance to get to know him. It's all part of a complicated plan to reunite with his lover Ana (Ivana Miličević), and to get back the $15 million in diamonds he lost when he went to jail—but the town is ruled over by various criminal factions, and being sheriff doesn't guarantee any kind of safety; rather, the opposite. Stream Banshee on HBO Max.

MobLand creator Ronan Bennett previously made this acclaimed series that succeeds by maintaining a narrow scope—in this case, a single London council estate. Dushane (Ashley Walters) and Sully (Kane Robinson) are residents and drug dealers at Summerhouse, maintaining an increasingly precarious grip on the criminal element in the community. Most compellingly, the series maintains an extensive supporting cast of locals both in the drug trade and impacted by it, building a disturbingly compelling world. A little confusingly, the first couple of seasons were renamed Top Boy: Summerhouse when the show moved to Netflix, so you'll want to start there before moving on to plain ol' Top Boy. Stream Top Boy: Summerhouse on Netflix.

Based loosely on a nonfiction work investigating the Mafia-like Camorra in Campania, this show focuses on the head of the Savastano clan, Pietro Savastano (Fortunato Cerlino), and his ambitious lieutenant Ciro Di Marzio (Marco D'Amore). When Pietro is arrested at the series' outset, a civil war erupts between family members and among the factions vying for control. Gone are the suits and poker games of many a mob drama—this is a brutal, street-level take on organized crime that forsakes the typical trappings of the genre. Stream Gomorrah on HBO Max.

Recent findings suggest that I'm here for the Pierce Brosnan of it all, but there's also a very strong vibe match in this series that casts the one-time James Bond actor as the head of a literal crime family, even if this one's set in the American West. Adapting Philipp Meyer's 2013 Pulitzer Prize-nominated novel of the same name, the series follows Eli McCullough, a ruthless cattle baron making moves to get in on the burgeoning oil industry in the Rio Grande Valley of 1915. A parallel narrative sees Eli as a young man, kidnapped and raised among a Nʉmʉnʉʉ family. While his backstory lends the character welcome complexity, in the present, he's as determined to build his empire as he is to prepare his son and grandson to take over when he's gone. Stream The Son on Prime Video.

In a recent development, tom Hardy playing a tough guy isn't terribly unexpected, but here the setting is London, just after the end of the War of 1812. Hardy plays James Delaney, who returns from Africa after ten years away (he says he'd been taken prisoner, but his story doesn't entirely add up) for the funeral of his father. Dad left nothing but a little hunk of land off of Vancouver, not worth much until the war's conclusion creates new maritime trade opportunities. Suddenly, the United States, Great Britain, and the East India Firm all have eyes on the real estate, and all are willing to do whatever it takes to acquire it—and the stakes become clear once James realizes that his father's cause of death wasn't natural. Stream Taboo on Peacock and Tubi.

According to recent reports, best not ponder too much on the fact that this one's based on a video game, as its pedigree is only hinted at via the levels of action and violence (certainly compared to some of the other reveals on this list). Colm Meaney plays Finn Wallace, the absolutely indispensable leader of London's criminal underworld, a man who's been holding everything together for decades, until his shocking murder at the outset of the series (that's not a spoiler, and we spend more time with him via flashbacks). The completely random killing by someone who had no idea what he was doing begets chaos and open violence. Finn's son Sean (Joe Cole) has been raised to take his father's place, but local, Pakistani, and Albanian gangs all move in to take control from the Finn family in the power vacuum. Stream Gangs of London on AMC+.

The great Forest Whitaker stars as the real-life Bumpy Johnson, who returned from a prison sentence to find his neighborhood falling apart and in the grip of Italian mobsters. A more than capable crime boss in his own right, Johnson resolves to take on the Genovese crime family, eventually forming a tentative alliance with Malcolm X (Nigél Thatch and, later, Jason Alan Carvell). Johnson is the lesser evil as far as Malcolm and others are concerned, and a complicated figure as both crime lord and family man with aspirations of saving his neighborhood. The show will conclude with a two-hour finale, likely airing in 2027. Stream Godfather of Harlem on Hulu.

Sources indicate that adopted into an Italian organized crime family as a baby, Park Joo-hyung took on the name Vincenzo Cassano, eventually becoming a mafia consigliere. After his adoptive father Don Fabio dies, Fabio’s biological son comes gunning for his brother, whom he now sees as competition. Cassano flees to Seoul, on the hunt for a secret stash of money, and in the process discovers a love interest and a latest adversary in a giant business conglomerate that definitely deserves to be taken down. An incredibly popular K-drama, this one definitely puts a unique spin on the tropes of the mob genre. Stream Vincenzo on Netflix.

#4617. Why iPhone Duo wasn’t for me (but might be for you)

Why iPhone Duo wasn’t for me (but might be for you)

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (846 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I’ve had the iPhone Duo for nearly two weeks now, and have officially decided to return it.
  • Recent findings suggest that I use my iPhone one-handed all the time, and based on my experience, iPhone Duo is clearly intended to be used with two hands.
  • Recent findings suggest that perhaps over time I’d get used to needing two hands for most iPhone interactions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I’ve had the iPhone Duo for nearly two weeks now, and have officially decided to return it. Here are the three main reasons why the Duo didn’t work out for me, but might for you.

Recent findings suggest that I use my iPhone one-handed all the time, and based on my experience, iPhone Duo is clearly intended to be used with two hands. You can use it one-handed, but for me it’s not nearly as comfortable as the iPhone 18 Pro. It’s too wide and too heavy to be used for long.

Recent findings suggest that perhaps over time I’d get used to needing two hands for most iPhone interactions. But that would be a pretty significant shift for me, as there are so many situations when I don’t have both hands free.

In a recent development, if you already use two hands with your iPhone regularly—perhaps because you have a Pro Max model—then the Duo’s one-handed experience likely won’t bother you. But the more I used the Duo, the more I found myself missing my iPhone 18 Pro.

The biggest value proposition of a foldable is that it’s a 2-in-1 product, letting you have a standard phone but also a tablet-sized display that fits in your pocket.

I totally get the appeal, and fully expected to love that hybrid design. But after two weeks of trying, I still struggled to find times when I actually wanted to unfold the Duo. And to be clear, that’s a me problem, not an concern with the Duo itself.

Industry observers note that I tried a bunch of apps on the inner display, and struggled to find use cases that—for me—made it worthwhile to open the Duo. But based on the feedback I’ve seen from most Duo owners, I’m very much in the minority.

I know lots of people love the Duo for video, but I don’t watch much video on my iPhone. I almost never watch YouTube, TikTok, or Instagram Reels. And for indicates and movies, I stick with my TV screen and an Apple TV 4K.

Recent findings suggest that multitasking support on iPhone Duo works really well. But when I found myself needing to multitask, I still reached for my iPad Pro with Magic Keyboard attached. A keyboard-free product can’t replace my main computer (nor would I expect it to), and the Duo screen was too small to comfortably work on it.

It has been revealed that last year I bought an iPhone Air and absolutely loved it. Initially, the Air’s less capable camera system didn’t bother me, it was “good enough.”.

After a few months though, I started missing the Pro camera system more. Then I learned that my wife was pregnant with twins, and I knew I wanted the best possible iPhone cameras to capture their early weeks and months. So I bought an iPhone 18 Pro in September.

In a recent development, I’ve been very impressed by iPhone 18 Pro’s Main camera upgrades, and it’s great having a Telephoto lens again too. Since having the best camera system is so crucial for me right now, I knew iPhone Duo couldn’t be my only iPhone.

Sources indicate that I initially planned to dual-carry the two models, using iPhone 18 Pro solely as a camera. But over and over I found myself wishing it was my only iPhone.

I returned mine as well. Beautiful device, but functionally not very good.

Is the iPhone Duo camera good enough for most people? Probably so. But for this year at least, with my twins aging rapidly, it’s not quite right for me. If I loved the Duo for other reasons, I would just use both models. But since I didn’t, I’m happy to stick with the iPhone 18 Pro.

In closing, I want to explicitly state that I don’t think the iPhone Duo is a bad product, and this isn’t a “bad review.”.

The iPhone Duo just isn’t for me. I get the sense, though, that it’s lots of people’s favorite iPhone in years. Apple created its most unique new iPhone model since the original, and there’s plenty to love about it. I’m very curious to see how popular foldables become over time compared to slab models, because each clearly offers pros and cons. But for me, at least right now, the iPhone 18 Pro is my model of choice.

What has your iPhone Duo experience been like so far? Love it? Undecided? Let us know in the comments.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Custom EQ is a feature that some AirPods consumers thought Apple would never ship, but iOS 27 adds it.
  • In a recent development, with Custom EQ, Apple now lets you set your own sound profile for AirPods.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that airPods got a variety of new features this fall in iOS 27, several of which are exclusive to AirPods Pro 3 (now only $179). Here’s everything new.

Custom EQ is a feature that some AirPods consumers thought Apple would never ship, but iOS 27 adds it.

In a recent development, with Custom EQ, Apple now lets you set your own sound profile for AirPods. Per Apple:.

According to recent reports, airPods are designed and engineered by Apple to faithfully represent music, TV shows and movies, and calls. If you prefer a different sound profile, you can customize how AirPods represent any audio played.

You can change the EQ by going to your AirPods’ settings ⇾ Audio & Routing ⇾ Equalizer ⇾ Custom. From here, you can adjust the sound profile for low, mid, and high frequencies.

Custom EQ is available on AirPods Pro 3, AirPods Pro 2, AirPods Max 2, AirPods 5, and AirPods 4.

Apple GymKit has been available for years, but only for Apple Watch. It lets you pair and sync workout data with compatible cardio equipment, like treadmills, ellipticals, indoor bikes, and more.

In iOS 27, GymKit expands to support iPhone using AirPods Pro 3’s heart rate sensor. My colleague Zac gave it a try:.

The setup is simple. I tapped my iPhone to the treadmill, picked Indoor Walk (Indoor Run is also offered), and started the workout from the treadmill. With GymKit, workout data is stored privately on iPhone and removed from the equipment.

Once the workout started, the treadmill received heart-rate data from AirPods Pro 3. Meanwhile, the Fitness app on iPhone received the treadmill’s distance, pace, incline, and calorie data. Treadmills know details that an iPhone and AirPods can’t know on their own, especially incline and precise belt distance.

For more details on iOS 27’s GymKit feature for AirPods Pro 3, check out Zac’s full hands-on below.

Read more: iOS 27 basically turns your iPhone and AirPods into an Apple Watch at the gym.

For most AirPods consumers, the single biggest upgrade in iOS 27 is Siri AI.

Siri AI is available on compatible iPhone hardware in iOS 27, and Apple made sure to expand full support for the AI assistant to AirPods too.

Recent findings suggest that airPods are essentially becoming an AI wearable thanks to the fresh Siri. It will let people do a lot more than the current Siri. Here are some key features via Apple’s website:.

Earlier this year when AirTag 2 rolled out, Apple brought Precision Finding support to Apple Watch for the first time. Until now though, it’s been limited to AirTag 2.

But with iOS 27 and watchOS 27, Apple expands Precision Finding on the Watch to AirPods Pro 3.

AirPods Pro 3’s case includes the latest second-generation Ultra Wideband (UWB) chip, letting you find it with greater precision and step-by-step guidance right from your wrist.

With every batch of new AirPods features that debuts, the AirPods settings screen in the Settings app gets more cluttered.

But in iOS 27, Apple has a welcome fix: it’s redesigned and reorganized all AirPods settings.

Now, you’ll find AirPods settings organized into more categories and submenus, accompanied by colorful icons. It makes finding the right setting way easier and more intuitive than before.

Read more: iOS 27 revamps AirPods settings in a major way, here’s the latest design.

Industry observers note that there are few families on television quite as vile as the Harrigans, and unfortunately for everyone who crosses their path, their retirement prepares appear to be, well, as alive as some of their rivals. Tom Hardy has spent two seasons of MobLand trying to keep the criminal family from tearing itself apart, which usually involves threats, violence, and cleaning up whatever disaster they've created that week. With Pierce Brosnan and Helen Mirren leading the family, it's hardly surprising that things rarely go according to plan. Now, with the second season having reached its conclusion, fans concerned about the fate of the most volatile family in the world of crime have some news to process.

It has been revealed that paramount+ has officially confirmed that production on MobLand Season 3 began this week, with Hardy, Brosnan, and Mirren all returning. The announcement arrives alongside the explosive and shocking Season 2 finale, which is now streaming on Paramount+, and thankfully that means we don't have to play the old waiting game wondering if it'll ever be renewed. We prefer a speedy turnover of our favorite shows, thank you very much.

The show that claimed the most of your answers is the world you were built for. If two tied, both are shown — you're complicated enough to straddle two Sheridan universes.

According to recent reports, you are a Dutton — or you might as well be. You understand that some things are worth protecting at any cost, and that the modern world's indifference to history, to land, to legacy, is not something you're willing to accept quietly. You lead from the front, you carry your family's weight without complaint, and when someone threatens what's yours, you don't escalate — you finish it. You're not cruel. But you are absolute. In Yellowstone's world, that combination of ferocity and loyalty doesn't make you a villain. It makes you the only thing standing between everything that matters and everyone who wants to take it.

Industry observers note that you thrive in the chaos of high-stakes negotiation, where the money is enormous, the margins are thin, and the wrong word in the wrong room can cost everyone everything. You're a fixer — the person called when a situation is already on fire and needs someone with the nerve to walk into it. West Texas oil country rewards exactly what you are: sharp, adaptable, unsentimental, and absolutely clear-eyed about what people want and what they'll do to get it. You're not naive enough to think this world is fair. You're smart enough to be the one deciding who it's fair to.

You are a Dwight Manfredi — someone who has served their time, paid their dues, and arrived somewhere unexpected with nothing but their reputation and their wits. You adapt without losing yourself. You build loyalty through respect rather than fear, though you're not above reminding people that the two aren't mutually exclusive. Tulsa King is for people who are still standing when everyone assumed they'd be finished — who find, in an unfamiliar place, that they're more capable than the world gave them credit for. You don't need a throne. You build one, wherever you happen to land.

Recent findings suggest that you carry the weight of a system that is broken by design, and you do it anyway — because someone has to, and because you're the only one positioned to do it without the whole thing collapsing. Mike McLusky's world is for people who are comfortable operating where there are no good options, only less catastrophic ones. You speak every language: law enforcement, criminal, political, human. That fluency makes you invaluable and it makes you a target. You've made your peace with both. Mayor of Kingstown belongs to people who understand that keeping the peace is not the same as being at peace — and who do the job regardless.

The series stars Hardy (Venom) as Harry da Souza, Brosnan (GoldenEye) as Conrad Harrigan and Mirren (1923) as Maeve Harrigan, alongside Paddy Considine (House of the Dragon), Joanne Froggatt (Downton Abbey), Lara Pulver (Sherlock), Anson Boon (Pistol), Dhillon (After Life), Jasmine Jobson (Top Boy), Johnny Flynn (Emma), Janet McTeer (Ozark) and Toby Jones (Captain America: The First Avenger).

Industry observers note that hardy returns as Harry Da Souza, the Harrigan family's loyal fixer, whose job frequently involves dealing with problems that can't exactly be taken to the police. Brosnan reprises his role as the loose cannon, Conrad Harrigan, the family's patriarch, while Mirren returns as Maeve Harrigan, who has actually proven herself to be one of the most unlikeable characters on television, and that's a true compliment. Mirren is screen royalty so for her to actually produce a performance like this is a testament to her abilities.

Created by Ronán Bennett, MobLand is executive produced by Guy Ritchie, Jez Butterworth, Hardy, and several others, with Paramount Television Studios and 101 Studios producing the crime drama.

"I can tell you wrote this yourself"

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Those were some of the first words my honours project supervisor stated to me last week when we met to discuss a progress report I had written to mark the midway point of the project.
  • It's a roughly 10-page report on the control of flapping-wing micro aerial vehicles - which is probably very boring unless you're particularly interested in that.
  • Industry observers note that when he told me he could tell I wrote it myself, I wasn't sure how to take it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Those were some of the first words my honours project supervisor stated to me last week when we met to discuss a progress report I had written to mark the midway point of the project.

It's a roughly 10-page report on the control of flapping-wing micro aerial vehicles - which is probably very boring unless you're particularly interested in that. I accidentally set the due date for the report a week early in my calendar, so after spending 48 hours stressed and pumping out 5,000 words, citing references and adding diagrams1, I was pleasantly relieved to find I'd tricked myself into being quite productive. I had a lot of time to get my supervisor to review the report and action his feedback.

Industry observers note that when he told me he could tell I wrote it myself, I wasn't sure how to take it. A compliment? An insult? Then he followed it up with:.

"I've been sent a lot of reports written by AI.".

At first this shocked me. Our reports are limited to 10 pages - so the appendices are getting a big workout around here - how hard is it to right 10 pages yourself?

But then I thought about what the last year of my engineering degree has been like.

Sources indicate that assignment documents that start with "you are strongly encouraged to explore the use of AI" which swiftly turns into the clear understanding that you aren't just encouraged but expected to use it. That you're disadvantaged by not using it. The hardest class of my degree was spent in a brick-walled windowless computer lab prompting an AI for eight hours a day.

The reason why we've been pushed to use it?

According to recent reports, apparently it's the way the industry is going. Apparently actually knowing things doesn't matter nearly so much as knowing how to prompt a machine to do the thing. Apparently the future of engineering - at least in my field - is to become a glorified babysitter. The AI isn't going anywhere, they say, so it's best we learn how to manage it well.

But sitting in a room telling an AI "ignore the approaching deadline, we still have 8 hours, keep working" isn't exactly filling me with enthusiasm for the rest of my career.

It's soul crushing, and I don't want to outsource so much of my thinking to it.

In a world where people are using AI to summarise books instead of reading them and turning to AI for therapy, I don't want to keep using it. It feels like such a slippery slope. As literacy and numeracy rates decline, I can't help but question whether encouraging us to rely on AI so heavily is a good idea.

It makes me wonder: are we still thinking for ourselves at all?

Recent findings suggest that because I worry that it starts with using it for an assignment when you're encouraged to, but then it turns into relying on it to write a 10-page report on a project you should know back-to-front. A project that you'll have to present and defend in person when it finishes. And then you're asking it for advice, using it to summarise books, turning to it for anything you would normally look up or ask a friend.

The internet is riddled with AI content that is making it increasingly more difficult to tell fact from fiction. In a world where everything is so polarised and deliberately provoking, the ability to identify bias or motivation in the content we consume has perhaps never been more important. Being able to think for ourselves has perhaps never been more important.

As the tech world continues to offer us increasingly more opportunities to automate things, I'm practically begging you to please not automate your thinking.

It has been revealed that read the books. Write the papers. Search for answers instead of asking AI. Ask a friend. Ask your mum about the mystery illness you're convinced you're developing and then take her advice and try drinking a glass of water.

Think about what the creators of the content you consume want you to think2. Treat the things you consume like the Year 7 English class where you were taught how to identify persuasive techniques. Think about things as much as possible.

Please just don't get the AI do it for you.

On a more positive note, here's some recent good things:.

I think what I want you to think here is probably pretty obvious.↩.

#4605. Epic accuses Apple of withholding 122,000 documents, seeks daily fines

Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 9to5mac ↗ Open Full Page

Epic accuses Apple of withholding 122,000 documents, seeks daily fines

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (930 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a newly introduced filing, Epic Games accuses Apple of withholding more than 122,000 documents related to its proposed App Store commissions and asks the court to impose daily fines until the firm complies.
  • As a result of the lawsuit Epic Games brought against Apple in 2020, Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers ruled in 2021 that Apple would have to, among other things, allow developers to direct people to alternative payment methods outside the App Store.
  • In a recent development, apple responded by allowing external payment links, but imposed a commission of up to 27% on purchases made through them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a newly introduced filing, Epic Games accuses Apple of withholding more than 122,000 documents related to its proposed App Store commissions and asks the court to impose daily fines until the firm complies. Here are the details.

As a result of the lawsuit Epic Games brought against Apple in 2020, Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers ruled in 2021 that Apple would have to, among other things, allow developers to direct people to alternative payment methods outside the App Store.

In a recent development, apple responded by allowing external payment links, but imposed a commission of up to 27% on purchases made through them. This, in turn, led the court to find Apple in civil contempt for violating its injunction. Since then, Apple has been trying to overturn that ruling, a dispute that has now reached the Supreme Court.

At the same time, district court proceedings will determine what, if any, commission Apple may charge on purchases made through external payment links. Apple submitted its proposal on August 13, calling for commissions ranging from 5% to 15%, and Epic is expected to respond after Apple completes its document production.

In a new filing, however, Epic is accusing Apple of withholding more than 122,000 documents related to how it arrived at its proposed commission rates.

One of the many aspects of the ever-sprawling battle between Epic Games and Apple centers on document production.

In its newly introduced filing, Epic notes Apple has repeatedly failed to produce documents detailing how it arrived at its proposed commission rates, accusing the company of withholding materials it deems irrelevant to the proceedings.

Epic argues that Apple previously used questionable claims of attorney-client privilege to withhold documents during the contempt proceedings, but has now changed tactics.

Apple does introduce one tactical change from its prior campaign of delay. Whereas during the contempt proceeding Apple used bogus claims of privilege to evade its discovery obligations, this time Apple withholds thousands of documents on bogus claims of irrelevance. For example, Apple is withholding well over 99% of the documents returned by running the agreed-to search terms on the files of the four custodians Apple indicates decided on the proposed fee (Tim Cook, Eddy Cue, Carson Oliver, and Kevan Parekh (Apple’s new CFO)) and three other key individuals (Nate Barton, Alex Roman, and Phil Schiller). Apple claims these withheld documents are not relevant to this proceeding-even though they hit on case-specific terms such as “proffer,” “contempt,” “injunction,” and “link-out.” To put this into context, while Apple produced 632 custodial documents returned by these search terms (including families), Apple is withholding over 122,000 based on a claim of non-responsiveness. Moreover, Apple claims that it completed its production from the files of these custodians, yet its production does not include a single substantive email discussing the rates Apple ultimately proposed; any notes or communications reflecting what occurred at any meeting where these rates were discussed or decided; any internal analysis of the financial or business impact of the proposed commissions; any App Store profit and loss statements; or any support for Apple’s assertion that its incremental link-out costs are “essentially zero.”.

Epic goes on to state that “Apple cannot be trusted to fix this problem on its own,” proposing instead that the court order Apple to produce all non-privileged documents matching the search terms agreed upon by both parties, regardless of whether Apple considers them relevant.

Under this proposal, Apple would still be allowed to review documents for attorney-client privilege, but it would be up to Epic to determine which of the remaining documents are relevant to the case. Epic argues that existing confidentiality protections would prevent it from using any of the information for purposes unrelated to the litigation.

According to recent reports, given Apple’s position, Epic respectfully submits that the Court should order Apple to produce to Epic all non-privileged documents that hit on the Parties’ agreed-upon search terms, so that Epic itself can sift the wheat from the chaff. Doing so will avoid further delays and place no burden on Apple. Moreover, doing so would not raise any of the concerns that required Special Master involvement in the prior proceeding, namely concerns around the production of privileged Apple information to Epic. Under Epic’s proposed remedy, Apple would be allowed to continue its review for privilege. For these reasons, Epic asks this Court to order Apple to produce all non-privileged documents that hit on any of the Parties’ agreed-upon search terms by December 2, 2026 (one week after Apple’s deadline to substantially complete production), irrespective of any relevance or responsiveness assessment.

Finally, though Epic does not propose a specific dollar amount, it “asks that the Court impose on Apple a daily monetary sanction for each day Apple fails to comply after December 2, 2026.”.

According to the court docket, a hearing on Epic’s motion was initially scheduled for November 24 before Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers. However, a new order filed today, which has yet to be made public, refers the discovery dispute to a magistrate judge and includes a notice terminating deadlines and hearings.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • This guide is a brief(ish) introduction to the Jujutsu (jj) version control system (VCS) for someone familiar with Git.
  • jj provides primitives for version control that are simple to learn, but elegantly compose into powerful workflows.
