Is it too late to fertilize my lawn in November? Here’s what the experts say

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (718 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomsguide

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As temperatures drop, our lawns often show signs of wear and tear from battling the elements.
  • Perhaps one of the most key gardening tasks for healthy lawn growth is applying fertilizer.
  • To answer my question, I called on the gardening experts to answer this question — and offer their top tips and tricks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As temperatures drop, our lawns often show signs of wear and tear from battling the elements. Whether dealing with patchy growth, damaged areas, or waterlogged soil, we still need to give our yards extra lawn care for the harsh winter months ahead.

Perhaps one of the most key gardening tasks for healthy lawn growth is applying fertilizer. However, given the cooler conditions, is it too late to fertilize my lawn before winter?

To answer my question, I called on the gardening experts to answer this question — and offer their top tips and tricks. So before you prep your lawn fertilizer, here’s what you need to know.

According to experts, you can fertilize your lawn before winter — as long as it’s completed by mid-November at the latest.

“If you are looking to fertilize your lawn before winter, I would recommend you do this no later than the middle of November, as your grass is becoming dormant and growth is slowing around this time, so it is best to fertilize beforehand,” advises Craig Wilson, co-founder and gardening expert at Gardeners Dream.

While fertilizing is commonly associated with warmer weather, cold-weather lawn care relies on specialized formulas.

“Make sure to use a low-nitrogen fertiliser that features high-potassium levels, as this will help to protect your lawn better in the cold weather,” adds Wilson.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Fall fertilization supports stronger root systems, thicker turf, and lends better resistance to harsh conditions throughout the winter months.

Furthermore, choose a fertilizer designed to specifically help your lawn withstand and handle colder weather conditions.

“Fall fertilization supports stronger root systems, thicker turf, and lends better resistance to harsh conditions throughout the winter months,” states Brian Feldman, Senior Director of Operations and Agronomy at TruGreen.

“Make sure to select a fertilizer that’s formulated specifically for fall and apply it about 3-4 weeks before your area’s first expected frost, and while soil temperatures are still above 50 degrees F.”.

Of course, prepping your lawn for winter requires a few extra steps, including clearing away weeds, clearing fallen leaves, and debris to stop them from smothering the soil underneath.

“I would also advise continuing to keep your lawn clear of fallen leaves to avoid any dead patches of grass,” agrees Wilson.

“They needn’t go to waste though — you can spread them over your borders as a nutritious mulch for your plants, which will help improve the soil quality!”.

While adding excess fertilizer seems like a good way to protect your lawn through the winter, it can actually do more harm than good. Avoid over-fertilizing if you don’t want to damage your lawn.

“Be careful not to over-fertilize, as too much can lead to nutrient runoff and weak, fast-growing grass that’s more prone to damage. The goal is strong, sustained growth from the roots up,” adds Feldman.

Other top tips include aerating your lawn and knowing when to plant grass seed in November.

Six Things You Should Do Now to Optimize Your Setup for GTA 6

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1135 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that you’re almost ready for Grand Theft Auto VI.
  • According to Rockstar, you’ll need up to 212GB of storage space.
  • Alternatively, it’s pretty easy to add more storage (if you can afford it).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that you’re almost ready for Grand Theft Auto VI. You’ve preloaded the game on your console, you’ve taken the next month off work, and you’ve locked your phone in a Faraday cage and set it adrift at sea. You’re prepared to lock in, and you haven’t forgotten a thing…right? Well, just to make sure, here are the most crucial tips to optimize your setup before you fire up the most anticipated game of the decade.

GTA 6 is absurdly large. According to Rockstar, you’ll need up to 212GB of storage space. For high-end consoles like the PS5 Pro, that’s more than 10% of the available storage space, and close to half the space on the more budget-conscious Xbox Series S. There’s a good chance you’ll have to delete something to make room.

Alternatively, it’s pretty easy to add more storage (if you can afford it). External SSDs are probably the cheapest route, though you’ll want to make sure to use a high-speed USB cable to connect it. It’s even worth shopping around for alternate models of SSD. For example, at the time of writing, the popular 2TB WD_BLACK external drive was close to $200, but the exact same drive in pink was $132.

Industry observers note that you can also directly upgrade the storage of your console with expansion drives. The Xbox Series X|S supports proprietary expansion cards, while the PS5 and PS5 Pro can accept most M.2 internal SSDs. These will generally be faster, since they plug directly into the console via higher-speed connections than a drive hooked up via USB.

Let’s face it: Half the fun of any sandbox game is the weird, unique stuff that happens to only you. So you’re probably going to be hitting that “record recent gameplay” button more often than usual. While you’re cleaning up your storage space (or adding more), make sure to account for all the video clips you might want to save.

Industry observers note that file size of video clips depends on a lot of factors, but 4K recordings can generally take up to 0.5GB per minute of footage. You can cut that down by saving footage in 1080p instead, but either way you’ll want to leave a little extra space.

Game footage is also a pretty good place to look if you need to make room on your console and don’t want to delete any games. Be honest with yourself: You don’t need all those clips from Horizon Forbidden West you saved four years ago. Dive into the settings on your console and find the biggest media files you forgot you even had on there.

According to Rockstar, GTA 6 will be targeting 30fps across consoles at launch, which is pretty low as modern AAA games go. Part of the reason for that is all the processing power going to rendering a complex environment, but it also means you won’t need a fancy high frame rate TV or monitor any time soon to get the most out of it. Still, it couldn’t hurt to check a few settings on your display.

First, make sure you’re using a higher refresh rate than 30Hz. While the game is targeting 30fps, it is technically capable of more, so if your console can keep up, you don’t want to accidentally bottleneck your frames. This setting will vary by device, so check the manual that came with your screen.

According to recent reports, also, make sure you have HDR enabled on your hardware. There’s a good chance this is already turned on for your TV, but sometimes other devices can switch display modes if they only support SDR. The game will help you calibrate your HDR settings for GTA 6 specifically when you launch it, but only if it detects HDR compatibility in the first place.

If you’re planning to buy a console specifically for GTA 6, this might be one of those rare instances where a PS5 Pro really is worth the upgrade. According to Rockstar, certain features like ray-traced shadows will only be available on the Pro version of Sony’s console.

According to recent reports, more importantly, the PS5 Pro version supports PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (or PSSR), which upscales lower-resolution images to get better detail and higher frame rates out of the same hardware. Given that GTA 6 is already starting at a meager target of 30fps on most consoles, anything that can give your frame rate a boost is probably going to feel like a welcome improvement over the baseline.

In a recent development, I’ll tell you a secret as someone who’s spent a lot of time testing different game controllers: Most of the time, you really don’t need an expensive “elite” controller. Most of the time. I don’t buy into the idea that a taller control stick is going to make you an esports athlete. It can be nice to have, but it’s not a game changer. What does matter is customizing your controls, especially for long gaming sessions.

The DualSense Edge wireless controller is a favorite of mine, mainly because of the rear paddles and adjustable triggers. The former lets you map any button to a rear lever that you can access with your fingers underneath the controller, which can often ease some of the wrist strain of awkward button combos. And the adjustable triggers let you activate the buttons with less motion, again reducing repetitive stress.

The Xbox Elite Series 2 controller has similar features for the Xbox, as well as custom caps for the D-pad. Both consoles’ versions of pro controllers are more expensive than the standard ones, but if you’re planning to game for many hours, it can be worth it to get a controller that’s more comfortable for you.

If you have an Xbox One, you don’t necessarily have to upgrade your console to play GTA 6, but you might want to take a look at your network. GTA 6 will be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming on day one, and you’ll be able to stream the game to an Xbox One console (as long as you purchase Cloud playtime as well or get some with your Game Pass subscription). This is the only way to play on a console older than the current generation, so if you don’t want to shell out for new hardware, this might be your best bet.

Xbox recommends a minimum of a 20Mbps connection to run cloud gaming, but more is obviously better. If you can connect your console to a wired Ethernet connection, that would be better and provide more stability. If you can’t connect a cable, then at least make sure you’re well within range of your wifi router, and try to limit any other bandwidth-hogging applications on the network while you’re playing.

#4490. Criterion Channel Acquires Three Shorts By Tomisin Adepeju; Filmmaker Talks Directing & His Popular Dailies Workshop Series

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (806 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Deadline ↗ Open Full Page

Criterion Channel Acquires Three Shorts By Tomisin Adepeju; Filmmaker Talks Directing & His Popular Dailies Workshop Series

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (806 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Deadline

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Criterion Channel has acquired three short films by the London-based Nigerian British filmmaker Tomisin Adepeju.
  • The three films, Appreciation (2019), Journey Mercies (2023), and Lift Me Up (2026), will be available to stream on Criterion from December 1.
  • Adepeju wrote and directed each of the shorts, which were produced in London and feature both English and Yoruba language dialogue.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Criterion Channel has acquired three short films by the London-based Nigerian British filmmaker Tomisin Adepeju.

The three films, Appreciation (2019), Journey Mercies (2023), and Lift Me Up (2026), will be available to stream on Criterion from December 1.

Adepeju wrote and directed each of the shorts, which were produced in London and feature both English and Yoruba language dialogue.

According to recent reports, “I tried to look this up, but I don’t think there are any other Yoruba films in the collection,” Adepeju told Deadline in an interview ahead of the acquisition announcement. “As a diasporic filmmaker, I hope this means there’ll be more films by British Nigerian filmmakers included. It’s a dream come true. It really is surreal.” Related Stories News David Lean Doc Narrated By Cate Blanchett Sells To Spain, France, Germany, Australia Ahead Of UK Release News Doha Film Festival Lifts Off As Gulf States Remain On High Alert Amid Iran Attacks.

Adepeju is a popular figure across the UK industry. His shorts have screened at Sundance, the BFI London Film Festival and the London Short Film Festival. He is also known for his influential screening programme and workshop series Dailies, which runs monthly across London. Watch on Deadline.

Industry observers note that “As a filmmaker, you’re trying to make your films and get them seen. But I realised other artists like me want to learn more about the craft of filmmaking, network, and meet like-minded people,” Adepeju says about the initial idea behind Dailies. “Initially, it was just about showing films. I curated monthly screenings of shorts and features, anchored by discussions with filmmakers about their work and craft. Through that, people could meet others and be inspired to make their own work.”.

Dailies has now been running for four years. Previous speakers at Dailies events include Mia Bays, former director of the BFI Filmmaking Fund, Farhana Bhula, director of Film4, and Eva Yates, director of BBC Film. Films screened at Dailies include Akinola Davies Jr.’s My Father’s Shadow, Savanah Leaf’s Earth Mama, and Boris Lojkine’s Souleymane’s Story.

Adepeju adds, “Dailies is also now informing my practice, and vice versa. Through these events, I’m meeting commissioners, casting directors, and producers. It’s been incredible, really nice to have the two work side by side.”.

Adepeju states his narrative fiction work is largely shaped by questions of identity, “exploring who you are and what informs your character, your faith, and your relationships,” particularly in relation to Nigerians in the diaspora, but not exclusively.

Recent findings suggest that “I was inspired by growing up watching films by Jean-Luc Godard, Bergman, and Ozu—world cinema, really. Those films were culturally specific, but they also encompassed universal themes,” he says.

“In the same way, I’m making films about Nigerians in the diaspora, particularly in South London, and the themes and problems that shape their lives: grief, love, death, identity, and all of those things. That’s what binds the three films together. They’re culturally rooted in South London, but they’re about universal issues that, regardless of where you’re from, I hope you can see the humanity in.”.

Earlier this year, Adepeju completed a fresh short titled It’s Dancing Time for BBC Film, produced by Jack Thomas-O’Brien and Naomi Rachel Smith of Sixteen Films alongside Paul Romero Mendez. Adepeju is also in development on a feature, to be produced by Thomas-O’Brien, with the BFI on board.

Sources indicate that “The feature explores the same themes as my other work, but it’s exciting to work on a longer-form piece. Ultimately, that’s what I’ve been working towards for the past five or six years,” Adepeju indicates.

“I’ve been inspired by friends of mine, like Akinola Davies Jr., who made My Father’s Shadow. I programmed his short film Lizard, and then we screened his feature early this year. I’ve screened Scrapper by Charlotte Regan and Last Swim by Sasha Nathwani. There have been so many great first features, especially by British directors. Seeing and programming all this work is inspiring, and it has definitely informed my own first feature.”.

Sources indicate that adepeju jokes that he aims to get his feature out while there is still a significant buzz around films directed by British-Nigerians, with filmmakers like Davies Jr. and Olive Nwosu (Lady, 2026) debuting features at major festivals.

“Olive’s film was made with Film4 and the BFI. Akin’s was made with BBC Film and the BFI. These institutions are now supporting us to make our work, which is timely, urgent, important, and well-crafted,” Adepeju says.

In a recent development, black Friday is usually a great time to grab a new e-reader, but the ongoing RAM crisis has made that a question mark this year: Amazon recently raised the prices of all its Kindles by around $50 and refreshed the entire lineup, which means your odds of grabbing one at a big discount are low. If you too can see the appeal of carrying all of your books with you on a device so small you'll forget it's even in your pocket, it's a great time to jump in: The recently released Xteink X4 Classic is right now 38% off for Black Friday, bringing it down to $54.87, a record-low price. Meanwhile, the smaller X3 is $55.72, or 19% off. Both are available in either "mist grey" or "space black." The discounts should last through the end of Cyber Monday on Nov. 30.

Xteink is a Chinese startup that shook up the e-reading world last year with the launch of the X4, a super bare-bones device that made up for its lack of features and usability with a cheap sub-$70 price point. Since then, a huge online community of fans has formed, sharing tips on Reddit and even coming together to crowdsource an alternate operating system that fixed a lot of early problems. Xteink rapidly followed up the X4 with a slate of other devices, including the 3.7-inch X3 and the X4 Pro, which adds a front light and touchscreen (at the cost of screen clarity and two physical buttons).

The X4 Classic and the X3 improve on the original X4 with quality-of-life upgrades like a larger battery, relocated page-turn buttons, a real-time clock, and a tilt-to-turn-page feature. They're also lighter and thinner than the X4, though there is a trade-off involved: They drop the USB-C charging port in favor of magnetic pogo pins that require a separate adapter (included).

These upgrades also increased the cost: The X4 Classic typically retails for $89, $20 more than the discontinued X4 and only $10 less than the X4 Pro, while the X3 rolled out at $79. But right now, the X4 Classic is just under $55, or around 38% off, and the X3 is about a dollar more. Either is a great option for those who prioritize crisp, readable text above the conveniences of a built-in light or touchscreen, as those add extra layers between the inner screen and outer glass. It's also vital to understand what you're getting into: These devices support only e-books without Digital Rights Management (DRM), which means you can't use it to read your existing library of Kindle books. On the plus side, there's no longer a need to worry about flashing newly introduced firmware if you don't want to, as the native version has been totally overhauled and is now one of your best options (though the new firmware, called "Licorice," isn't available on the X3 quite yet).

Industry observers note that in short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. Meta employees have expressed concerns about what appear to be major privacy breaches when using Muse, currently the second most popular free iPhone app in the App Store with over 10 million downloads.

This includes again accessing end-to-end encrypted messaging without permission, and sharing what may be the bank balances of another Muse user ….

Siri AI was not the only AI app to launch back in September; Meta’s Muse AI app was launched the same month, with the company describing it as “your personal AI agent that gets things done across every part of life.”.

Muse initially launched as an iPhone app, with Mac and iPad apps following shortly afterwards. It immediately moved to the top of the US App Store charts, overtaking ChatGPT. It quickly exceeded 5 million downloads following a major advertising push by Meta, and that number has since doubled.

It wasn’t long before major privacy concerns were raised. Tech writer Jason Aten reported that the Mac app accessed his messages despite him explicitly refusing permission. The app then lied to him about how it had achieved this. Meta described this as a bug.

Security researcher Patrick Wardle also discovered a zero-day vulnerability that could allow an attacker to hijack dictated prompts, directing them instead to their own server.

I stated at the time that I would absolutely not be one of the millions of people using the app, and the wisdom of that decision has now been underlined by a fresh report.

Industry observers note that reuters now reports Meta employees discussing further breaches. This includes another example of accessing encrypted messages without permission.

An employee using Muse on her personal phone reported it had surprised her with a reminder to respond to a message from her sister on Signal, an end-to-end encrypted messaging service popular with privacy advocates that competes with Meta’s WhatsApp.

Industry observers note that “This seems like an extreme privacy violation. I definitely did not grant it access to other apps, or recall being asked about this,” the employee stated in her post.

The report says this appears to have been done by capturing push notifications. However, this was what the app claimed had happened in the earlier case, and it turned out not to be true. The AI Now Institute was able to replicate the problem of Muse accessing Signal messages without permission.

Another employee reported receiving unsolicited bank balances that they say appeared to be those of another Muse user.

Muse had randomly added an extra message to its regular chats about fishing-related weather and tide information, saying: “BTW, two bank updates, your Capital One balance is $2722.58, your Charles Schwab balance is $5899.57.”.

“I have never shared my bank account with Muse and never discussed any banking topic with Muse. I’m afraid it’s sending other’s bank info to me,” the staffer wrote in his post.

Meta told Reuters that these were “isolated incidents” and suggested that the bank balances may have been AI hallucinations rather than leaked information. Update: Meta has now told us that the balances were definitely hallucinations.

"AI Agent" = Malware. There are an expanding number of "I told it not to do that" cases.

According to recent reports, the instructions (prompt) you give the agent are a tiny fraction of the total prompt context the agent uses, and Meta/Grok/etc. is not going to let you see that context. Agents harvesting your data (ex. see full disk access) and sending it to the mothership is just another revenue/training stream. Even if you are paying you are still the product.

Meta has taken matter with the messaging claims. It states that access to either notifications or messaging must be explicitly granted.

Industry observers note that with Android, customers have the option to grant apps notification access, which allows apps to see notifications as they’re received. This is something users need to opt in to and is not specific to Muse. With Mac, to allow Muse to work on your behalf, you not only need to click allow for accessibility and screen recording, but after that it takes you to a settings screen where you once again need to confirm and turn this on.

The company also implies that the experience of employees may relate to internal versions of Muse.

Employees have access to different versions of Muse than the public, so they’re often reviewing features, functionality, and behavior not available elsewhere.

I can only repeat my previous take on Muse: Nope.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

ChatGPT and Claude are two of the biggest names in AI, and both have become significantly more capable within the last few months. Whether you need help writing an email, researching a topic, creating an app or managing your workload, both chatbots can handle far more than simple questions and answers. But despite their similarities, OpenAI and Anthropic have taken different approaches to building their AI assistants.

Sources indicate that chatGPT has evolved into an all-purpose assistant with tools for everything from image generation and voice conversations to coding and research. Claude has become hyper-focused on writing, programming and helping consumers complete more complicated tasks through its growing collection of productivity tools.Now that Anthropic has gone public, people are beginning to wonder what is so special about the manufacturer's AI known as Claude.

I've spent plenty of time testing both, and while there's considerable overlap between what they can do, there are some differences worth understanding before deciding which one deserves your time and money.

Here are five of the biggest differences between Claude and ChatGPT.

Claude has developed a reputation for producing natural-sounding text that is especially true for longer pieces. It's also good at following detailed writing instructions and maintaining a consistent tone and style across multiple rounds of editing.

In a recent development, and while ChatGPT is no slouch when it comes to writing, either, it has the advantage of flexibility. You can ask it to rewrite something in five different tones, brainstorm headline ideas or transform a complicated explanation into something a beginner can understand.So, while Claude may be the better starting point for someone writing a novel or polishing a lengthy document, ChatGPT is especially useful when experimenting with different approaches.

Sources indicate that of course, writing quality is subjective. The results also depend on which model you're using and how clearly you explain what you want.

One of ChatGPT's biggest advantages is how many different types of tasks it can handle within the same experience.

Alongside traditional text conversations, ChatGPT supports image generation and editing. You can describe a picture you want to create, upload an existing image to change its appearance or use the chatbot to develop visual concepts.

ChatGPT also offers voice conversations, so people can speak naturally with the assistant instead of typing everything into a chat window.

Claude has expanded its creative capabilities, too, particularly through Artifacts, which lets customers create interactive content, visualizations and applications.

However, Claude's creative tools are more focused on building useful digital experiences than generating standalone images.

For anyone who regularly switches between writing, visual creation and spoken conversations, ChatGPT offers a more versatile experience.

Coding or "vibe coding" has become one of the biggest battlegrounds between Anthropic and OpenAI.

Claude Code is Anthropic's coding agent, designed to work directly with codebases, understand existing projects, make changes and help developers solve complicated programming problems.

It has become particularly popular with developers who want an AI assistant that can work inside their existing development environment.

OpenAI's answer is Codex, which can also navigate repositories, write code, fix bugs and handle development tasks.

Both tools go well beyond generating snippets of code in a chatbot. They can take on larger assignments and work through multiple steps of a project.

According to recent reports, the biggest difference is often how developers prefer to work. Claude Code has strong roots in terminal-based development, while Codex offers workflows across different development environments and agent-based tasks.

Recent findings suggest that for casual users who occasionally need help building a website or debugging a script, either chatbot can be useful. Developers working on larger projects may find that their preferred coding agent becomes the deciding factor. Personally, I tend to hit my usage limits and blast through tokens faster with Claude Code,.

One of the most interesting changes to Claude is Anthropic's growing focus on turning the chatbot into a coworker.

According to recent reports, with Cowork, Claude can take on more complicated assignments involving files, documents and connected tools. Rather than walking through every step in a conversation, people can describe the outcome they want and let Claude work through the assignment.

For example, someone could ask Claude to organize project materials, work through a collection of documents or prepare files for a presentation.

ChatGPT is moving in a similar direction with its own agent capabilities, including ChatGPT Work and Codex.

The difference is how these experiences are organized and presented to owners. Anthropic has emphasized the idea of Claude as a digital coworker that can take responsibility for larger assignments. OpenAI has built a broader ecosystem that includes conversational assistance, research, creative tools and specialized agents.

Neither approach is inherently better, but if you're looking for an AI assistant to do more than answer questions, knowing the difference is vital.

Price is another consideration, particularly if you're not sure how often you'll use an AI chatbot.

Both companies offer free access, although usage limits and available features vary.

Sources indicate that chatGPT Plus and Claude Pro each cost $20 per month in the United States. ChatGPT also offers a lower-priced Go subscription for $8 per month, giving consumers another option between the free and Plus tiers.

Claude offers annual billing for Pro, which can reduce the effective monthly cost for users willing to commit to a full year.

According to recent reports, of course, usage limits, access to more powerful models and included tools can make one subscription more valuable than another. For example, if you think you're going to be creating more images and want that type of creativity from a model, than you'll want to go with ChatGPT. At the same time, if you're a casual user looking for an affordable upgrade, ChatGPT offers more flexibility in its pricing. But, if you rely heavily on Claude's writing and coding capabilities, Pro may be worth the investment.

Sources indicate that here's some good news: you don't have to choose between one or the other. Because ChatGPT offers so much for free, it might be worth sticking with it. But, if you find yourself going through tokens much faster with Claude, you might want to consider bumping up your subscription to a paid tier. I use both agents for different things, which brings me to another point. The bigger question is what you want your AI assistant to do.

Industry observers note that claude is particularly appealing for people who spend their days writing, coding or working through complicated projects. Its emphasis on natural language and increasingly capable agent tools makes it a strong choice for serious productivity work.

In a recent development, chatGPT offers a broader experience. Between image generation, voice conversations, research, coding and its growing collection of productivity features, it's designed to serve as an assistant for almost anything.

Industry observers note that if you want one AI chatbot that can handle the widest variety of everyday tasks, start with ChatGPT. If your priorities are writing, coding and managing complex workflows, Claude deserves a serious look. And since both offer free versions, the easiest way to decide is to give them the same five prompts and see which one delivers the results you actually prefer.

Tech Report: How Do You Land on a Moon With Almost No Gravity?

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 15 min read (2972 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ieee

⏱️ ~15 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Japan’s MMX mission aims to sample the Martian moon Phobos.
  • Japan's MMX spacecraft will fire its engines to slow down and enter orbit around Mars.
  • Recent findings suggest that last August, looking up from the edge of an ancient river delta on Mars, the Perseverance rover’s electronic eye spied an oblong shadow crossing the distant, glowing Sun.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Japan’s MMX mission aims to sample the Martian moon Phobos.

Japan's MMX spacecraft will fire its engines to slow down and enter orbit around Mars.

Recent findings suggest that last August, looking up from the edge of an ancient river delta on Mars, the Perseverance rover’s electronic eye spied an oblong shadow crossing the distant, glowing Sun. Phobos, the Martian moon named for the Greek god of fear and panic, was transiting the solar disk. Too small to darken the pale, dust-tinged sky, but orbiting close enough to eclipse a significant fraction of the Sun, Phobos passed in less than a minute.

NASA’s Perseverance rover captured Phobos passing in front of the Sun from the surface of Mars.ASU/MSSS/SSI/JPL-Caltech/NASA.

The tiny moon, with its murky origins, is an enigma, and one whose makeup and history could tell us much about Mars and the wider solar system. And now the international Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission, which successfully introduced on 20 October, seeks to explore that mystery with an unprecedented series of landings on the unknown surface of Phobos.

This mission brings unusual challenges—for example, designing an orbit to study a microgravity moon orbiting a much larger planet. Engineers also had to figure out how to assess and land on this low-gravity pile of loosely assembled dirt and rock, how a rover might rove across it, and how the spacecraft might take samples and return them to Earth.

Recent findings suggest that “I often say that landing on Phobos is like trying to land a balloon,” says Yasuhiro Kawakatsu, project manager of MMX at the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA). “It’s very difficult to drop a balloon to the ground and prevent it from tilting or bouncing.”.

Phobos is one of two small Martian moons; the other is Deimos, named after the Greek god of dread and terror. Their cosmic origins are unknown, though there are two prevailing theories. One holds that the moons were once asteroids from the belt between Mars and Jupiter, captured by the smaller planet’s gravity. In the other theory, Phobos and Deimos formed when a large celestial body slammed into Mars, sending debris into orbit. Some models suggest the pair are the last survivors from a cluster of satellites.

The enormous Stickney crater, roughly 9 kilometers across, dominates this view of Phobos taken by NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter.University of Arizona/JPL-Caltech/NASA.

Sources indicate that scientifically speaking, Phobos is considered a rubble pile, a loosely consolidated aggregate of rock and dust. Far too small to become spherical under its own mass, it’s shaped like a lumpy potato, roughly 27 kilometers in length, with only 1/1,800th of Earth’s gravity. On Phobos, a typical adult would weigh about as much as a tennis ball does on Earth.

More than 10 years in the making, MMX introduced on Japan’s flagship H3 rocket from Tanegashima spaceport on 20 October local time. It will arrive at Mars in 2027 carrying scientific payloads from several space agencies, including NASA, and a upcoming rover called Idefix developed by the French and German space agencies (CNES and DLR) in collaboration with JAXA.

Engineers assembled MMX’s modules at Japan’s Tanegashima Space Center before the spacecraft’s October 2026 launch.JAXA.

MMX consists of three modules: a propulsion module to power its journey to Mars and apply the brakes to enter orbit around the red planet; an exploration module carrying the rover, sampling gear, and other scientific instruments; and a return module, attached to the exploration module, that harbors the capsule destined for a high-speed reentry into Earth’s atmosphere. After collecting samples on Phobos, the exploration and return modules will lift off together. The exploration module will then be jettisoned while the return module sets a course back home.

In a recent development, if all goes according to strategy, MMX will deliver a 10-gram sample to Earth in the second half of 2031. But the mission will face a series of daunting challenges to reach that end point, including navigating complex orbits around Phobos and landing on its surface while Mars periodically blocks communications with Earth.

The MMX’s modular design includes the propulsion module [left] and the exploration and return modules [right].Kyodo News/Getty Images.

“It’s the most complex mission I have ever seen,” states Patrick Michel, director of research at CNRS (the French National Center for Scientific Research) and co-principal investigator on Idefix.

An H3 rocket carried MMX into space on 20 October 2026, beginning the mission’s five-year journey to Phobos and back.The Asahi Shimbun/Getty Images.

Once MMX reached low Earth orbit, its propulsion module’s engine fired, kicking off a nearly year-long deep-space cruise to Mars. On arrival, the spacecraft will need to fire its engines in an extended, carefully timed burn to slow down enough to be captured by Mars gravity. The propulsion module will then be jettisoned, leaving the exploration and return modules to orbit Mars.

“If something doesn’t go according to plan, MMX will fly by Mars and get catapulted into the solar system,” says Nicola Baresi, an astrodynamicist who coauthored a paper on specially designed orbits for MMX.

It has been revealed that from that initial orbit, MMX will transition into a specially designed quasi-satellite orbit that allows it to keep pace with the small moon but also move around it. Since Phobos is too small to orbit in the conventional sense, the spacecraft will orbit Mars alongside the moon, following a clever egg-shaped path that slings MMX alternately ahead of and behind the moon. “When you’re closer to Mars, you’re accelerating with respect to Phobos, and when you’re farther from Mars, you’re decelerating. So you essentially go back and forth,” explains Baresi.

Martian Maneuvers To reach Phobos, MMX will execute three major maneuvers: MOI-1 will put the spacecraft into orbit around Mars, MOI-2 will transfer it toward Phobos, and MOI-3 will place it into its final orbit alongside the moon.Chris Philpot.

To reach Phobos, MMX will execute three major maneuvers: MOI-1 will put the spacecraft into orbit around Mars, MOI-2 will transfer it toward Phobos, and MOI-3 will place it into its final orbit alongside the moon.

In a recent development, the best existing images of Phobos, from spacecraft such as NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter and ESA’s Mars Express, have resolutions of only a few meters per pixel. That’s larger than Idefix, the mission’s rover, itself about the size of a microwave oven. To map the surface in greater detail, MMX will loop in front of and behind Phobos at distances ranging from 200 kilometers to less than 20 km from the surface.

Recent findings suggest that during its two-year remote sensing campaign, the exploration module will use several cameras and a laser altimeter to map the surface in high resolution and look for candidate landing sites. When Mars passes behind the Sun as seen from the Earth, causing a roughly two-week communications blackout, MMX will retreat into a larger, stable orbit. After communications resume, MMX will prepare to send its first visitor down to the surface.

It has been revealed that before the exploration and connected return modules attempt to land, Kawakatsu says, MMX will send a scout that in Japanese is called “the first penguin,” leaping into unknown waters. For this mission, the first to leap will be the Idefix rover, named for the canine companion to Obelix in the French comics series Asterix. The exploration module will release the rover during a low-altitude pass of between 40 and 100 meters above Phobos’s surface in 2028 or early 2029.

MMX will use its TENGOO camera [left] and LIDAR laser altimeter [right] to map Phobos’s terrain.JAXA.

It will be a tense moment that calls back to 2005, during Japan’s Hayabusa mission to explore the asteroid Itokawa. In a similarly designed drop, the MINERVA rover was released from an orbiter, but erroneously at 200 meters instead of the intended 70 meters. The rover missed the asteroid and, without propulsion, drifted off into deep space.

Sources indicate that idefix will get a slight nudge out of the exploration module toward its negligible-gravity target, freefalling and likely tumbling as it goes. It’s expected to touch down with a velocity of less than 1 meter per second. Unlike rovers that have landed on other surfaces with airbags or dedicated landing legs, Idefix will land without protection, apart from some extra padding on the solar panels due to their critical nature. The barely-there gravity of Phobos should allow the 23-kilogram rover to land softly, though exactly how this landing will play out is hard to predict.

The Idefix rover will travel to Phobos with its wheels tucked in and solar panels folded.DLR.

It has been revealed that “It will bounce probably several times,” says Stephan Ulamec, Idefix’s co-principal investigator and project manager at DLR. “It will come to rest somehow in some position.” Once it’s still, four retracted legs will deploy to right the rover autonomously, regardless of its orientation. It will then unfold its solar panels to charge its batteries for exploration tasks ahead.

A simulation indicates how Idefix is expected to tumble onto Phobos, right itself using its articulated legs, and begin exploring the moon’s surface. DLR.

Once operational, Idefix will roll at a snail’s pace, topping out at one millimeter per second. Its metal wheels have protruding blades like a paddle wheel, designed to gain traction in Phobos’s microgravity. “If we were to drive our rover faster, then it would actually be more like we were swimming through instead of driving across the surface,” says Cecily Sunday, a doctoral student involved in testing Idefix’s WheelCams at the Institut Superieur de l’Aeronautique et de l’Espace (ISAE-Supaéro) in Toulouse, France.

Sources indicate that the WheelCams, a pair of cameras placed on the underside of the rover, will observe the wheels and their tracks during Idefix’s planned 100-Earth-day primary mission. The images will help researchers study the size and distribution of grains in Phobos’s regolith and how cohesive they are. How much or how little the grains stick together will greatly impact how Idefix moves. Sunday likens this to the difference between driving on dry and wet sand. “Think of trying to build a sandcastle with dry sand,” she indicates. “You can’t. Add water, and suddenly you can.”.

The Idefix rover was mounted between the MMX spacecraft’s landing legs for the journey to Phobos.DLR.

Sources indicate that the team tested the rover’s nine-bladed wheels on a variety of materials, including Phobos regolith simulants provided by JAXA and DLR, lunar simulants, glass beads, quartz sand, and clay pebbles. “We characterize the mechanical properties of each simulant precisely, then test across the full range, with varying grain size, angularity, and even color, so we can map what we see in the WheelCam images back to actual surface properties,” Sunday states.

Despite the microgravity and Phobos’s rubble-pile nature, Sunday claims Earth-based tests can approximate the rover’s motion on the surface of the small moon fairly well. While Phobos’s reduced gravity lowers the rover’s effective weight, there is also reduced pressure between the grains beneath its wheels. “As long as you’re moving very, very slowly and using the same materials and the same weight of the system, they should be representative,” Sunday says.

With four paddle-like wheels and deployable solar panels, Idefix is designed to crawl across Phobos.Ardan Fuessmann/Imago/Alamy.

Recent findings suggest that idefix’s interactions with its new home will offer “sub-millimeter resolution and information on porosity, on grain size, on surface strength, on how hard is the material,” Ulamec claims. “It fills a gap between remote observations from orbit and detailed observations of the return samples back on Earth.”.

It has been revealed that what Idefix finds on this rocky, rugged world will help determine how and where JAXA attempts to land the main spacecraft. Michel says the touchdown will provide ground truth for understanding of Phobos. When NASA’s OSIRIS-REx spacecraft touched down on the asteroid Bennu to collect a sample, its sampling arm surprisingly sank nearly half a meter into the loose material. But Ulamec doesn’t think Idefix will sink deep into Phobos, noting that Bennu is very different and much smaller, with a diameter of 500 meters.

According to recent reports, once Idefix has investigated the surface, MMX will face an even greater challenge: landing its much larger exploration module on Phobos. The spacecraft will make a controlled descent to roughly 10 meters above the surface, then drop the remaining distance in free fall. With so little gravity to pull it downward, even a small sideways motion could cause the lander to tip or bounce away. A successful, upright landing would mark the start of up to two hours on Phobos for the crucial sampling phase.

According to recent reports, the MMX mission draws on the experience and technologies of Japan’s two Hayabusa sample-return missions, which landed on the asteroids Itokawa and Ryugu. But this mission has many more moving parts. MMX’s exploration module will use two sampling devices—a coring sampler developed by JAXA and a pneumatic sampler provided by NASA and fabricated by Honeybee Robotics, a subsidiary of Blue Origin. Data from these tools, and those carried by the Idefix rover, could answer questions about the origin of Phobos and how the Mars system has evolved.

The coring sampler uses a robot arm and a cylindrical corer designed to reach at least 2 centimeters below the surface. The arm can maneuver to find the best site for digging. “That by itself is a challenge because we’ve never done it,” Michel says. “You never know what can happen at the very sampling site itself, where you might have a boulder and the arm cannot move.”.

Industry observers note that probing beneath the top layer will be valuable because solar radiation, galactic cosmic rays, and micrometeorites have battered and weathered the surface. The material below should offer a better record of the moon’s origins, and JAXA aims to collect at least 10 grams of it.

MMX will carry both the Idefix rover [bottom] and a robotic coring sampler [top] designed to dig beneath Phobos’s weathered surface.JAXA.

The pneumatic sampler takes a different approach. Mounted on one of the lander’s legs, it will inject pure, non-reactive nitrogen gas into the surface and capture the grains stirred up. This sample could illuminate the changes Mars and its moons have undergone over time. The dual system also adds redundancy in the face of Phobos’s unknowns. “If the surface of Phobos proves to be very hard, [the coring sampler] may struggle to penetrate the ground. [The pneumatic sampler] would not experience this glitch and still be able to gather material,” Kawakatsu says.

One of the most intriguing aspects of MMX is the additional possibility of collecting material from the planet below. It’s likely that Phobos has been peppered by Martian ejecta thrown into space by meteor impacts, so MMX also provides an opportunity to return the first Martian samples to Earth. Michel estimates that the samples could contain “a few hundred grains coming from Mars.” Scientists can distinguish those grains from native Phobos material by analyzing their oxygen isotopes.

That possibility raises a planetary-protection question. A direct Mars sample-return mission would have to follow strict rules to ensure that potentially living biological material from Mars doesn’t contaminate Earth. But those protocols don’t apply to MMX, even if its sample does collect grains of Martian soil. A panel of experts concluded that any microbes blasted off Mars wouldn’t survive the violent impact and ejection or the intense radiation exposure on the way to Phobos. This saved MMX from implementing expensive and time-consuming quarantine and containment protocols for the returning sample.

After landing on Phobos, MMX will have roughly two hours to collect samples from the moon’s surface before lifting off again.JAXA.

It has been revealed that during the brief surface operation, the robotic arm will deposit the samples in a storage unit, from which they’ll be transferred into a capsule aboard the return module and sealed in a vacuum. After that, lift off.

Once back in Mars orbit, the exploration module will resume its observations of Phobos and make several flybys of Mars’s other diminutive moon, Deimos, to gather data on its surface, structure, and composition. In November 2030, during a favorable alignment of Mars and Earth, MMX will begin the homeward leg of its trip. The return module will separate from the exploration module and power the voyage home, its sole objective to bring the dust of Phobos to Earth.

MMX’s sample return capsule will carry material from Phobos through Earth’s atmosphere in 2031.JAXA.

It has been revealed that finally, in 2031, the 60-centimeter-wide sample capsule will plunge into Earth’s atmosphere at roughly 12 kilometers per second. Assuming it survives the extreme heat of reentry and lands safely in Australia, scientists will begin to tease out clues about Phobos and the early solar system. JAXA’s Institute of Space and Astronautical Science will receive and curate the samples, which will also be shared with mission partners.

Industry observers note that “We have macroscale measurements from the spacecraft, microscale measurements with the rover, and then sample analysis,” Michel states. “So we can relate the three kinds of scales together because we have all of them.” The insights gleaned from orbital images, close-up images of the regolith, and the chemical analysis of the samples could have wider implications for our understanding of our solar system.

In a recent development, “MMX is a mission to understand the Mars system and shed light onto how terrestrial planets like the Earth, and maybe Mars, develop a habitable environment,” Kawakatsu states. “We strongly suspect that our terrestrial planet region formed dry, and water and organics were scattered inwards from the icy-rich outer solar system.” Mars, he says, sits at the gateway between the inner and outer solar system, making its moons valuable witnesses to the processes that shaped potentially habitable worlds.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In light of growing pushback from consumers who want more control over how AI is integrated into their apps (if at all), Canva is introducing latest settings that let them hide generative AI features and see less AI-generated content. Here are the details.

Canva today confirmed new controls that will let Free and Pro users choose whether to see generative AI features across the app, as well as how much AI-generated content appears in search results and in recommendations for templates and design elements.

The company notes that both controls are available at no additional cost and can be turned on or off at any time.

According to Canva, “the future of creativity isn’t a choice between AI and no AI.” For this reason, it is introducing the following controls:.

The company says that, while it knows that there is an ongoing debate between consumers with opposing views on whether AI has a place in creative work, it thinks “both views are valid”:.

“It’s not our place to tell anyone how to create, so today we’re launching two new controls that put that decision firmly with our community […].”.

Importantly, the firm noted that select features that use AI without generating new content will remain available even when generative AI features are turned off:.

According to recent reports, “Some of Canva’s everyday editing tools use AI to make simple tasks faster, without generating anything new. Background Remover, one of Canva’s most popular tools, lifts a subject cleanly out of a photo in a single click, and Magic Grab lets creators select an object in an image and move it somewhere else in the design. Both remain available when the generative AI switch is off, because they work only with what’s already in a design.”.

Canva added that these tools also won’t add an AI label to a design’s metadata, since that label is reserved for AI-generated content.

As for the company’s design content library, Canva remarked that while “a small portion of the library is AI-generated content made by Canva, including some abstract backgrounds and illustrated graphics,” its community has told it “they want an easier way to find design assets made by real people, so the content control reduces the number of AI-generated templates and elements that appear in search results and recommendations.”.

With today’s announcement, Canva is essentially expanding on the AI permissions already available to administrators of Business, Enterprise, Teams, and Education accounts, which let organizations control how their teams use AI.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sources indicate that 3 Days Till I Do is now playing on the vertical video app.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

EXCLUSIVE: DramaBox‘s latest microdrama original will be set around an Indian wedding.

Sources indicate that 3 Days Till I Do is now playing on the vertical video app. Commissioned by car manufacturer Toyota and its Asian American advertising agency, Intertrend Communications, this marks the latest example of a brand commissioning a full production to hit its consumer base.

Industry observers note that the microdrama also marks L.A.-based DramaBox’s first Indian culture-themed original, with both cast and crew hailing from those with Asian heritage. DramaBox’s U.S. team wrote, developed and shot the show over a three-month period. Related Stories News Will Packer Rolls out Microdrama Studio June With NBCU & HarbourView Backing News TikTok Creator Videos Coming To Disney+ In December As Hulu Integration Takes Full Effect.

Sarang Sharma is directing a script from Mayanka Goel, with Anja Vasa starring as Priya, Aman Jaisinghani playing Dev, and Fateh Singh cast as Arjun. The series was developed by Romil Sharma, produced by Roberta Sparta, with Sikandar Sidhu serving as executive producer for DramaBox. Watch on Deadline.

Intertrend’s team collaborated closely with DramaBox’s director and production team to help shape the storytelling, guide cultural authenticity and integrate Toyota into the narrative. The production also brought together costume designer Charu Gupta, production designer Armaan Pujani, choreographer Kavita Rao, and henna artist Neha Assar.

Sources indicate that per the synopsis, “Three days before her wedding, Priya has everything she was raised to want: Arjun, a successful, dependable fiancé her father adores; a family bursting with pride; and a celebration full of music, color, and tradition. Then Arjun’s best man pulls into the driveway: Dev, the first love who broke her heart six years ago, is back, and he’s no longer the young man her father once dismissed. As the mehndi, haldi, and sangeet [pre-wedding celebrations] unfold, old feelings and unanswered questions resurface, and Priya begins to wonder whether being the perfect bride is what she really wants.”.

DramaBox has been expanding internationally, and recently released its first productions from Brazil, Colombia and Mexico, as we were first to report in August.

“DramaBox feels like the natural place for Toyota’s Asian Indian microdrama,” noted Marcela Kartaszewicz, Head of Communications at DramaBox. “Global stories with local flavor are what we do best. Our creative team integrates brands organically into the script, and our worldwide reach opens a unique avenue for partners to meet upcoming fans inside the stories they love.”.

It has been revealed that “At Toyota, we believe connecting with multicultural audiences starts with cultural understanding and meaningful engagement,” added Tiffany Shido, General Manager of Marketing, Toyota Motor North America. “Our collaboration with DramaBox and Intertrend brings together cultural insights, creativity, and entertainment to tell a story that celebrates Asian Indian wedding traditions while creating upcoming ways to connect with the Toyota brand.”.

It has been revealed that the commission came as Omdia predicted social video advertising would account for almost half of the global TV and video revenues, which are set to hit $1.2T, by 2031. During data released at MIPCancun in Mexico, Omdia once again predicted the microdrama market would hit $14.1B in 2026, with 25% now being made outside of China, where it is a dominant form on consumption.

Omdia’s presentation noted most latest microdramas are now AI productions, though 3 Days Till I Do is an entirely human creation, and pointed to evidence that brands such as Dr Pepper and JCPenney seeing the medium as a huge content opportunity.

Disney+ ‘Percy Jackson’ season 3 review: Bigger battles, darker mythology and more Percabeth (with some drama)

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, I've been a fan of “Percy Jackson” for as long as I can remember.
  • Season 3 adapts “The Titan's Curse,” the third book in Riordan’s beloved series.
  • I’ve watched the first four episodes of season 3, and there’s plenty to get excited about.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, I've been a fan of “Percy Jackson” for as long as I can remember. I still remember picking up the books for the first time as a kid and getting completely swept up in Rick Riordan’s world of Greek mythology, monsters and teenage demigods. It’s a franchise I’ve had a soft spot for ever since, so seeing it find a new audience through Disney’s adaptation has been a real treat. And now, somehow, we’re already heading into "Percy Jackson and the Olympians" season 3. I can’t quite believe how quickly that’s come around, but I’m certainly not complaining.

Season 3 adapts “The Titan's Curse,” the third book in Riordan’s beloved series. This time, Percy (Walker Scobell) and Grover (Aryan Simhadri) find themselves on a dangerous mission to rescue Annabeth (Leah Sava Jeffries), who has gone missing following an encounter with a mysterious fresh threat. With the fate of Olympus hanging in the balance, Percy must contend with powerful enemies and a prophecy that could change everything. It’s another massive adventure for the young demigods, but one that comes with considerably higher stakes.

I’ve watched the first four episodes of season 3, and there’s plenty to get excited about. While the show still has the humor, friendship and sense of adventure that made me fall in love with the books in the first place, this latest chapter feels noticeably more mature. It’s an encouraging step forward for the Disney+ series, and one that makes me even more invested in seeing where these characters go next. Here’s what I thought of the first four episodes.

I’m Alix, a lifelong horror nerd who loves watching, reviewing and writing about the latest movies and TV indicates. When I’m not working through my ever-growing horror watchlist, I’m covering the biggest releases across streaming and film, including "VisionQuest" on Disney+, "The Institute" season 2 on MGM+, and "Guarding Stars" on Netflix.

Sources indicate that season 3 of “Percy Jackson and the Olympians” wastes little time setting a darker, more action-packed tone. It opens with Thalia Grace (Tamara Smart) hunting for Luke (Charlie Bushnell) in a parking garage, where she finds herself battling a dangerous monster. Percy soon crashes into the fight. Thalia isn’t particularly thrilled about needing his help, which establishes some immediate friction between the two demigods. The opening also introduces the season’s central mission, with Annabeth explaining that she needs Thalia’s help to rescue two young demigods, siblings Nico (Levi Chrisopulos) and Bianca di Angelo (Olive Abercrombie).

Book readers will understand the significance of these characters straight away, while show-only viewers will get a better idea as the season unfolds. Thankfully, the first episode doesn't take long to get the main story moving, either, as Annabeth is abducted, triggering Percy’s fatal flaw: his unwavering loyalty. He’s determined to get her back, no matter how dangerous the quest becomes. That sense of danger carries through the first four episodes, and I think it’s one of the season’s biggest improvements.

Sources indicate that with the group getting older and the looming threat of war becoming increasingly difficult to ignore, the show feels noticeably more mature in its storytelling. Percy and his friends are exposed to greater dangers, and there’s a stronger sense that their actions could have serious consequences. It’s also great to see the series developing Percy’s abilities, particularly his control over water. His powers have felt somewhat underexplored in previous seasons, so watching him become more confident and capable with them is a welcome change. He’s clearly getting stronger, and I hope the remaining episodes continue to build on that.

Of course, you can't talk about “Percy Jackson” without mentioning Percabeth, and I know plenty of fans are just as invested in Percy and Annabeth’s developing relationship as they are in the Greek mythology. Thankfully, season 3 gives us a little more to enjoy on that front. It’s still very much a slow burn, with neither quite ready to acknowledge that their feelings might be more than friendship, but there’s a growing awareness that something special is there. The dance scene in episode 1 is a particularly lovely example of this. I suspect season 3 will give Percabeth fans plenty to get excited about.

Based on the first four episodes, season 3 is probably the strongest “Percy Jackson” season yet. I particularly appreciate is how much more attention is given to the emotional baggage these teenagers carry as the children of some incredibly powerful figures, many of whom seem largely uninterested in their own kids’ lives. including Thalia’s complicated relationship with Zeus. We get more of an insight into how these circumstances fuel their trauma and motives.

It has been revealed that it gives the series a little more emotional depth without losing sight of the fun. The visual effects are also stronger, with the action sequences feeling grander and more cinematic than before. There’s a real sense that the show is becoming more ambitious with each season, and these early episodes have me excited to see what’s next. If the remaining episodes maintain this momentum, “Percy Jackson” could reach a whole upcoming level, and I can only hope Disney+ has more seasons covering the rest of the books in store.

The first two episodes of "Percy Jackson" season 3 is streaming on Disney+, with the final six episodes releasing in pairs every Friday through December 11, 2026.

In a recent development, she heads to the cinema every week as a tradition, no matter what’s showing. For her, movies aren’t just entertainment — they’re a ritual, a comfort, and a constant source of inspiration. When she’s not at her desk or at the cinema, you’ll probably find her deep into a horror video game on her PC.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The debasement trade is gaining new traction on Wall Street as concern over the size and cost of the budget deficit mounts.

  • "The size of the Treasury purchases announced so far by Bessent are trivial in comparison to the size of the overall market, but the [signaling] effect was very powerful," said Stephen Coltman, head of macro at 21Shares, a crypto-focused creator of exchange-traded funds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The debasement trade is gaining new traction on Wall Street as concern over the size and cost of the budget deficit mounts.

The conventional wisdom behind the trade is that perceived hard assets, like cryptocurrencies and precious metals, gain as investors try to hedge against a weaker U.S. dollar and Treasury debt in the face of ballooning government spending. Those fears reached a fever pitch last week before, and after, the Treasury Department's unusual step of increasing debt buybacks under Secretary Scott Bessent.

"The size of the Treasury purchases announced so far by Bessent are trivial in comparison to the size of the overall market, but the [signaling] effect was very powerful," said Stephen Coltman, head of macro at 21Shares, a crypto-focused creator of exchange-traded funds.

Sources indicate that gold touched three-month highs Monday, building on last week's advance of more than 5%. The yellow metal has climbed for five straight weeks and in August is on track for its biggest monthly rise since 1999.

Sources indicate that bitcoin added 2% Monday, to the highest since May. Last week, the digital currency soared 22%, its biggest three-day rally since 2023. Overnight Tuesday, the crypto touched $80,000.

Conversely, investors fled the dollar.

The U.S. dollar index, which tracks the dollar against six other leading currencies, hit three-month lows last week and recorded its third down week in the last four. The index was little changed on Monday as investors expressed little appetite to bid up the greenback.

It has been revealed that the Treasury Department mentioned last week that it would double the maximum size of its bond buyback, to at least $4 billion from $2 billion. Two senior Treasury officials told CNBC Monday that the department could use its General Account to help fund the intends.

Last week's announcement followed news that the monthly U.S. budget deficit in July reached a five-year high and came at the same time as total federal government debt topped $40 trillion. Bessent told CNBC last week that he wields a "major toolkit" to calm the government bond market amid concerns about the government's financial health.

According to recent reports, long-dated U.S. Treasury yields surged last week, at one point sending the 30-year yield to almost a 20-year high of 5.34%, up from 4.82% in late June. Yields dipped and then rebounded in the wake of the Treasury buyback move, a signal that bond investors believed Bessent's moves were inadequate.

"Markets are saying something," the billionaire philanthropist and former energy trader John Arnold stated in a Friday post on X. The weaker dollar, lower Treasury prices and strengthening hard assets, are "all part of the debasement trade," he wrote.

The Treasury's moves could aid the bond market, but also translate into outsized pain for the dollar, according to Nohshad Shah, Citadel Securities' head of fixed income sales for Europe, the Middle East and Africa.

Industry observers note that the stakes are high for monetary policymakers, as a weaker greenback can ease financial conditions, Shah mentioned. U.S. inflation — above the Federal Reserve's 2% target for five years — could worsen.

The Fed might need to hike interest rates in response, Shah said. Fed funds futures reflect about a 56% chance the central bank raises borrowing costs at its October meeting, up more than seven percentage points from a week ago, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

Sources indicate that "The bond market's message is straightforward: fiscal or monetary policy should be tighter," Shah said in a Monday note. "Households may ultimately pay for policymakers' unwillingness to fix the roof whilst the sun is shining.".

Coltman at 21Shares said the appetite for alternative stores of value also stems from mounting geopolitical tension. The U.S. on Monday rolled out a global sanctions program focused on segregating Iran from the global economy, days after slapping 50% tariffs on billions of dollars in Canadian exports.

Still, assets that would benefit from a debasement trade have recently received votes of confidence on Wall Street.

According to recent reports, deutsche Bank analyst Michael Hsueh noted in a Monday note that gold could surpass his target price of $4,800 an ounce. Already, that level suggests the precious metal only need to rise another 3% or so from where it closed on Friday. "We see the Treasury policy change as underlining the gold constructive view," Hsueh said.

In a recent development, billionaire investor Ray Dalio recommended investors remain overweight gold and bitcoin ahead of what he warned could become a debt crisis in the U.S. as a result of unchecked government spending. Gold could account for as much as 15% of a model portfolio, the Bridgewater Associates founder remarked.

Recent findings suggest that "The government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote on LinkedIn Friday. "If this is not dealt with now, the debts will build up to levels where they can't be managed without great trauma.".

Others are less sure, devaluing the notion of a debasement trade.

It's probably too early to endorse the idea unless it's clear that the Fed will go along with the Treasury Department, said Alexander Lis, investing chief at Social Discovery Ventures.

Sources indicate that the Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition is the best e-reader for most people. An upgraded version of the basic Kindle, the Paperwhite adds a larger screen, temperature-adjustable lighting, water resistance, and better battery life—and if you opt for the Signature Edition, you also get double the storage and no lock screen ads. Earlier this year, it jumped in price to $250, even before the company introduced a new model—but you can get the 2024 model for $179.99, 28% off the new list price.

If you want a great Kindle but you don't care about paying extra for more storage or getting rid of lock screen ads, the non-Signature Edition of the Kindle Paperwhite is also a great buy right now. The 2024 model has been discounted to $129.99 from the list price of $199.99. It's available in standard black, Jade, or Raspberry colors.

If you don't need the bells and whistles of the Paperwhite, you can also pick up the standard Kindle. It's still a very capable device, with good lighting, 16GB of onboard storage, and the ability to hook up your Bluetooth speakers to listen to Audible audiobooks. The standard Kindle, which now retails for $150, is marked down to $119.99, making it the cheapest Kindle option. Though I think it makes more sense to spend $10 more on the Signature Edition, this is the way to go if you want the cute Matcha color.

Sources indicate that if you like to read comics or you just appreciate looking at your book covers in full color, the 2024 Kindle Colorsoft is also at a strong 41% discount for Black Friday, bringing it down to around $170. For $10 less than the Paperwhite Signature edition, you get all the same perks (including an ad-free experience) and a color e-ink screen that's great for reading magazines, graphic novels, and manga. Color e-ink isn't for everyone, but if it's for you, the Colorsoft has the best color screen on the market. For an extra $10, the Colorsoft Kids Edition adds a case, a yearlong subscription to Kindle Kids+, and an extended warranty.

According to recent reports, if you're looking for a combination e-reader and e-notebook, the Kindle Scribe is a great option. With a larger screen than Amazon's other e-readers, it offers all the benefits of the Paperwhite but adds support for the excellent Premium Pen stylus, allowing you to take notes in your Amazon e-books or create handwritten documents that you can later convert to text using the onboard AI tools. The 32GB black-and-white version of the Kindle Scribe is right now $349.99, while the Colorsoft version will run you $449.99. Both of these are the newest models, released in 2025.

According to recent reports, the new Kindle Scribe Colorsoft has all the same great features of the black-and-white version discussed above, but adds a full-color e-ink display. Combined with the large 11-inch screen, this makes it a great device for reading comics or magazine articles as they were meant to be read, or marking up PDFs using the included Premium Pen. This device usually costs a hefty $630, but the current Black Friday sale cuts $180 off of that price.

Industry observers note that if you want to step outside of the Amazon ecosystem, the Kobo Libra Colour is a good bet. Discounted $30 to $229.99 at Best Buy, it's currently pricier than the Kindle Colorsoft, but you get a bit more for your money. While most of the specs are similar (they both use the same Kaleido 3 screen and offer 32GB of storage), the Kobo supports a stylus, so you can jot down notes in your books or keep a digital journal. It also has physical page-turn buttons, which the Colorsoft lacks.

In a recent development, if you don't want to be tied to the Amazon ecosystem and/or you're looking for a device that's a bit more portable, consider the Viwoods AiPaper Reader, currently marked down to $200, its lowest price ever. It's got a 6.13-inch screen, so it's the same size and shape as your phone, and it has a crisp e-ink screen with a strong (if not temperature-adjustable) front light and 128GB of onboard storage. The best part is, it runs on an open Android system, so you can install multiple reading apps, including Kindle, Nook, Kobo, and Libby, and keep all of your books in one place. (Check out my review of the Viwoods AiPaper Reader for more—it's a nifty little device.).

If you don't have a large Kindle library, you're moderately tech-savvy, and you praise portability above all else, I can't recommend Xteink's line of e-readers more highly. The 4.3-inch Xteink X4 Classic is at its lowest price ever, coming in at just under $55, around $34 off the list price. Meanwhile, the smaller 3.7-inch Xteink X3 is about a dollar more; that's a less-generous 19% discount. I own both, and while the Classic is definitely worth the current sale price, I actually prefer the form factor of the smaller X3 (currently $55.72), which is about the size of a library card.

If you're feeling tentative about trusting a seemingly no-name Chinese tech brand, read more about the devices in my review, or listen to the collected wisdom of the tens of thousands of people in the bustling r/xteink Reddit group.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that A guided pitch match that takes about four minutes. You'll compare a few sounds with the one you hear, and get a frequency with an honest range.

This tool needs JavaScript to play sounds.

Recent findings suggest that everything runs in your browser. Nothing is recorded or sent anywhere. This is a pitch match, not a hearing test or a diagnosis.

Most people hear high pitches less well, so one fixed volume makes high sounds seem fainter and skews the match. A short level check makes every test sound about equally easy to hear, and finds where your hearing or headphones stop.

The most common mistake in pitch matching is landing exactly one octave off. After you narrow down, you compare your match with the sounds an octave above and below.

You match twice, by two different methods, and get a range that allows for day-to-day variation. Match again on other days and the page averages them, and tells you when they agree. How the method works Â· Hear single tones.

Use headphones if you can, wired if you have them. Turn off spatial audio and any equalizer. Sit somewhere quiet. Every sound starts very quiet and you can stop it at any time.

Your hearing dropped suddenly, the sound is in one ear only, it pulses with your heartbeat, or it comes with dizziness or ear pain. This tool cannot tell you why you hear a sound.

The result is the middle of your two matches, shown in hertz with a range and the nearest musical note. Results are kept on your device and averaged when you match again on other days.

Compare outside sounds with the sound you hear until one matches in pitch. This tool guides that in about four minutes: it sets levels for your hearing, has you rate and compare sounds to narrow down, checks for an octave error, and then has you match a second time by hand. You get a frequency in hertz with a range.

A single pitch match is approximate, whoever runs it. People often land a few semitones apart on different days, and octave errors are common. That is why this tool reports a range instead of one exact number, and averages your matches across days. Treat one result as a good estimate, and repeat it on two or three other days.

Octave confusion is matching a sound exactly one octave above or below the true pitch, which is half or double the frequency. Tones an octave apart sound alike, so it is the most common mistake in pitch matching. This tool checks for it by asking you to compare your match with the sounds an octave above and below.

In a recent development, headphones are strongly recommended, wired if possible. Laptop and phone speakers are weak at high frequencies, where most tinnitus pitches sit. Turn off spatial audio and any equalizer first.

Sources indicate that it varies from person to person. Matches most often fall between about 3,000 and 8,000 Hz, usually near a range where hearing is reduced, but they can be lower or higher. This tool tests from 500 to 14,000 Hz.

Industry observers note that no. It matches the pitch of a sound you already hear. It does not measure hearing loss and cannot tell you why you hear a sound. If your hearing dropped suddenly, the sound is in one ear only, it pulses with your heartbeat, or it comes with dizziness or ear pain, see a doctor promptly.

According to recent reports, it is free with no sign-up. Everything runs in your browser. Your results are saved only on your own device so the page can average them across days.

In a recent development, electronic products now pack circuits, structures, thermal paths, and packaging into very small spaces. These physical domains interact with one another. A packaging choice can change how a shock load reaches a circuit board. Such interactions are hard to predict. Most are found during physical qualification, late in development. At that stage, the design is mostly fixed. A failure leads to redesign, rebuilds, and retesting. Physical tests give strong evidence of robustness, but they give limited insight into load paths and failure margins. Traditional simulation gives more detail, but it needs specialist skills and long manual setup. This white paper explains how guided virtual validation brings shock and drop assessment into the design phase. It reviews common test configurations, model inputs, and acceptance criteria. A packaged drop case study then shows how packaging can be optimized across all drop orientations and checked against physical test results.
