💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, our relationships are foundational to our lives—our sense of safety and how we understand the world around us.
  • Goodnight Mommy definitely leans into the psychological horror aspect of an impostor mother much, much harder than Phony, but it’s just a deeper dive into the show’s darker implications (and, fair warning, this movie is dark).
  • A woman identified only as Mother returns from having cosmetic surgery with her face totally enveloped in bandages, and her twin sons observe strange differences in her behavior that convince them she isn’t their real mother—she appears to ignore one of her sons completely, and disciplines them much more harshly than before.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, our relationships are foundational to our lives—our sense of safety and how we understand the world around us. When someone close to us suddenly, imperceptibly shifts, it can be unsettling, especially because you can’t be sure what’s changed or why. Those are the waters where Hulu’s Phony swims, delivering a perfectly pitched dramedy about a teenager (Sam Nivola) who emerges from a brief coma convinced that his mother (a pitch-perfect Connie Britton) has been replaced with a double. If you loved the series (and similar shows) and you’re looking for more intriguing stories about doubles and impostors close to home, you should definitely watch Goodnight Mommy.

Goodnight Mommy definitely leans into the psychological horror aspect of an impostor mother much, much harder than Phony, but it’s just a deeper dive into the show’s darker implications (and, fair warning, this movie is dark).

A woman identified only as Mother returns from having cosmetic surgery with her face totally enveloped in bandages, and her twin sons observe strange differences in her behavior that convince them she isn’t their real mother—she appears to ignore one of her sons completely, and disciplines them much more harshly than before. The boys also find clues that bolster their fears, including a photograph showing their mother posing with a woman dressed identically to her.

In a recent development, the boys’ attempts to force her to confess rapidly descend into a kind of madness, ultimately leading them to tie her to the bed in an effort to force her to admit she’s not their real mother. It all leads to a reveal as affecting as Phony’s ultimate explanation (albeit a lot more grim and violent). The film goes way harder than the series, but if you were totally into the premise, this is the more horrifying version you’ll want to see. The original film is German; there was a 2022 remake starring Naomi Watts, and while it's pretty good, the original is the right choice. Stream Goodnight Mommy on Kanopy or Plex, or rent it on Prime Video.

Sources indicate that looking for more impostor stories that dig into the psychological and emotional impact of suspecting someone has been replaced? Here are a few more movies that dig into the concept.

It has been revealed that the Hole in the Ground offers an inversion: A mother who becomes convinced that her son has been replaced by an impostor. Firmly in the supernatural horror genre, the story still plays the same game with the viewer: Is Sarah (Seána Kerslake) crazy, or has her son, Chris (James Quinn Markey), been replaced by a creature living in the woods near their home? It’s got the same disturbing energy as Sarah struggles with how much her son’s changed behavior is her own psychological projection and how much is clear evidence that he’s no longer the same person—or, possibly, even the same species. Stream The Hole in the Ground on HBO Max or rent it on Prime Video.

Taking a slightly more literary approach (it’s based on a novella by Fyodor Dostoyevsky), The Double explores what happens if you find yourself replaced by a doppelgänger. Simon (Jesse Eisenberg) is a nonentity—ignored at work, lonely, and silently longing for the girl living across the street, Hannah (Mia Wasikowska). One day, a new employee named James appears at Simon’s job—and James looks exactly like Simon. But James is assertive, confident, and charming, sending Simon into a spiral. As the two versions slide into a battle for dominance, Simon finds himself turning to increasingly deranged moves to rid himself of the new and improved version of himself. If you loved the psychological implications that Phony explores, check out The Double. Stream The Double on Kanopy, Hoopla, or Tubi, or rent it on Prime Video.

It has been revealed that on one level, Denis Villeneuve’s 2013 film is about a college professor named Adam (Jake Gyllenhaal) who discovers an actor named Anthony who looks exactly like him (also played by Gyllenhaal). When he tracks his double down, their lives merge in messy ways, ending in tragedy and one of the most striking (and confusing) final shots in cinema history. On another level, Enemy is a deft trick, exploring someone’s subconscious using dream logic and misdirection. If the best part about Phony was the disorienting sense that a secret just under the surface will explain everything, Enemy is the perfect choice. Stream Enemy on HBO Max or rent it on Prime Video.

According to recent reports, if you’re looking for a deeper, crazier, and more terrifying story about doubles, Andrzej Żuławski’s 1981 film is a terrific choice. Inspired in part by his own feelings in the wake of a painful divorce, the story follows Mark (Sam Neil), a spy who returns to West Berlin at the height of the Cold War only to find out his wife, Anna (Isabelle Adjani), has been having an affair and wants a divorce. But Anna’s behavior becomes increasingly strange, and then Mark meets their son’s teacher, Helen, who looks just like Anna. And that’s before Anna kind of ... grows a replacement Mark from a tentacled creature kept in her bathroom (and that’s just the beginning of how weird this movie gets), resulting in two doubles. How much of the film is meant literally and how much simply represents the trauma of romantic betrayal and divorce is up to you, but Possession will definitely leave a mark. Stream Possession on Shudder, Kanopy, or Hoopla, or rent it on Prime Video.

According to recent reports, obsession looks at the Doppelgänger Effect from a different perspective. Cliff Robertson plays Michael Courtland, a wealthy businessman whose wife (Geneviève Bujold) and young daughter, Amy (Wanda Blackman), are kidnapped in 1959. When he follows police advice against delivering the ransom, both appear to be killed in an explosion. Courtland spends the next 16 years hating himself, until he encounters a young woman, Sandra (also Bujold), who looks almost exactly like his late wife. He works to make Sandra look as much like his wife as possible, and eventually proposes—but then Sandra is kidnapped in precisely the same way as his wife and daughter sixteen years before. This all leads to a head-spinning series of reveals and a twist that echoes the Hitchcock classic Vertigo. Rent Obsession on Prime Video.

The answer is this deeply discounted $22 Casio watch, which, on pretty much any other day, would cost you $64. Here are five reasons why.

Marked down from $64 to just $22, this retro-1990s Casio digital watch features an onboard step counter and Bluetooth antenna for automatic time adjustments.

Sources indicate that hidden behind the screen of this seemingly ordinary digital watch is a Bluetooth antenna. Why would a dumb watch need Bluetooth? To pair it with your smartphone, of course. Once paired, the Casio WSB1000 automatically corrects the time based on your smartphone’s clock.

This means there’s no need to fuss with resetting the time when traveling across time zones. The bare-bones smartphone app can also be used to set or cancel an alarm on the watch, a timer, a stopwatch, and other basic functions.

Lastly, the onboard Bluetooth plays a key role in this next feature.

Industry observers note that you’ll notice that the Casio WSB1000 has the words “Step Tracker” printed above the LCD. This refers to this little watch’s automatic step-counting feature. Who needs the best Apple Watch or the latest Fitbit?

Like an actual smartwatch or fitness tracker, users can set daily step-count targets. The WSB1000 not only tracks your total and displays it on the watch’s LCD, but it also reveals a dynamic graphic of your progress toward that day’s goal.

Bluetooth, meanwhile, is used to ping that step-count data back to your smartphone.

It has been revealed that with onboard Bluetooth and automatic step-count tracking, battery life must be pretty short? Surprisingly, no. Casio indicates that the common drugstore CR2016 battery in the watch should keep it powered for approximately two years.

Afterwards, a battery swap should be a relatively painless, affordable process, done either at home (if you're savvy) or at your local jewelry store.

While the Casio WSB1000 isn’t quite as durable as watches in the brand’s legendary G-Shock range, this digital wonder is rated for 100 meters of water resistance, the same as the latest Apple Watch Ultra 4. It also boasts a shock-resistant (though not shockproof), lightweight resin case.

Ultimately, for less than $25, you're not just getting a Bluetooth-capable digital watch with step counting; you're getting the Casio WSB1000, a 90s timepiece with a design that's Tom Cruise-running-atop-a-moving-train-cool; it's Keanu Reeves-stopping-a-speeding-bus-badass... etc.

And even if your intended recipient overlooks the step tracking and tosses this watch in a drawer for occasional use, when they do eventually pull it out and pop it on, you can be sure the time and date will be spot-on thanks to the Bluetooth connection.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple has three main Apple Watch "lines." There's the flagship, right now the Series 12, which represents Apple's mainstream wearable. For athletes and consumers who think they'll put their watches through some extreme scenarios, there's the Ultra line, currently the Apple Watch Ultra 4. And while both the Series 12 and Ultra 4 are excellent devices in their own right, they can be pretty pricey (particularly the Ultra). That's why the third category, the SE, is actually best for most people, and Lifehacker's choice for best smartwatch gift of the year. Better yet, the third-generation SE is currently $50 off ahead of Black Friday, perfect for most people asking for an Apple Watch this year.

The SE 3 does just about everything you'd expect an Apple Watch to do. It, of course, has a heart rate sensor to keep tabs on your pulse, including high and low heart rate alerts; the ability to track dozens of different workouts and exercise types (including swimming, thanks to the device's water resistance); a sleep tracker with daily analyses available in the Health app; notification forwarding to check in on your alerts without opening your iPhone; and the ability to send and receive text messages.

It comes in two sizes (40mm and 44mm) depending on how large or small you prefer your watch. No matter which model you get, the watch comes with the S10 chip, Apple's last-generation watch processor. While it isn't as fast as the current S11 chip, the S10 is more than capable of running watchOS 27. Apple says the SE 3 can run for up to 18 hours on a single charge, and up to 32 hours in Low Power Mode, with fast charging from 0% to 80% in 45 minutes.

The majority of the features missing from the SE 3 aren't essential. Apple's other watches have things like bigger, brighter displays, additional health tracking tools like hypertension alerts and an ECG sensor, longer battery life, and Audio Intelligence—the latter of which might be a benefit to miss, depending on who you are.

If your giftee wants or needs any of those additional features, Series 12 or Ultra 4 might be a better choice. But for anyone who wants the essential Apple Watch experience, the SE 3 is simply the best-value watch Apple sells right now—especially at this discount. Right now, the watch starts at $199 for the 40mm watch, or $229 for the 44mm. You can also save on the cellular versions of these watches: $249 for the cellular 40mm watch, and $279 for the cellular 44mm model.

UK court rules Apple can share the top secret order everyone already knew

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (763 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Investigatory Powers Tribunal – essentially a British court that deals with complaints about state surveillance – has ruled that Apple is allowed to reveal a secret order it received from the UK government.
  • Apple had already found a clever way to alert British customers to the classified order without breaking the law, but it can now confirm what we all already knew, and talk openly about the issue ….
  • According to recent reports, the story centers on Apple’s introduction of the Advanced Data Protection (ADP) privacy feature back in 2022.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Investigatory Powers Tribunal – essentially a British court that deals with complaints about state surveillance – has ruled that Apple is allowed to reveal a secret order it received from the UK government.

Apple had already found a clever way to alert British customers to the classified order without breaking the law, but it can now confirm what we all already knew, and talk openly about the issue ….

According to recent reports, the story centers on Apple’s introduction of the Advanced Data Protection (ADP) privacy feature back in 2022. This extended end-to-end encryption to almost all your iCloud data, meaning Apple has no access, and therefore cannot grant access to any government agencies who come knocking on its door.

Industry observers note that the feature is off by default because it means Apple cannot help you access any of your data if, for example, you forget your iCloud password. However, those who want to maximize the privacy of their iCloud account can enable it.

Industry observers note that in 2025, the British government ordered Apple to create a backdoor to allow access by security services and law enforcement. Even worse, the order was issued under legislation that prohibits companies from revealing that they have received this demand.

This would have meant that British customers who enabled ADP would think that their data was safe when in fact it wasn’t. As we’ve said many times before, any backdoor created for use by the good guys is vulnerable to discovery and exploitation by the bad guys.

It would have been illegal for Apple to reveal that it had been instructed to compromise the privacy of customer data, but the company found a clever way to effectively communicate this without breaking the law. Apple announced it was withdrawing ADP from the UK without explaining its reason.

Industry observers note that “Apple can no longer offer Advanced Data Protection (ADP) in the United Kingdom to upcoming consumers and current UK users will eventually need to disable this security feature. ADP protects iCloud data with end-to-end encryption, which means the data can only be decrypted by the user who owns it, and only on their trusted devices. We are gravely disappointed that the protections provided by ADP will not be available to our customers in the UK […] As we have stated many times before, we have never built a backdoor or master key to any of our products or services and we never will.”.

Tell me you’ve been ordered to create a backdoor to ADP without telling me you’ve been ordered to create a backdoor to ADP ….

At this point, it was an open secret. However, ridiculously, despite the fact that everyone in the security and privacy field knew about it and was talking about it, Apple was still not allowed to officially confirm it.

According to recent reports, the iPhone maker asked the Investigatory Powers Tribunal (IPT) to allow it to openly discuss the order, with privacy campaigners backing this call. The Financial Times reports that the court has now ruled in Apple’s favor.

It has been revealed that the UK government must admit that it issued a secret order to Apple to allow it access to encrypted customer data, a court has ruled […] The Home Office has “not established that it would be damaging to national security” to reveal that Apple had received a “technical capability notice” (TCN), the tribunal said. The ruling means that […] “much” of Apple and the non-profits’ legal challenge can now take place in open court.

One of the great ironies is that most people had never heard of ADP until the government effectively made it headline news in the tech press three years after it rolled out – a classic example of the Streisand Effect.

This ruling is a win both for transparency and commonsense. To be clear, the actual requirement for a backdoor remains in place, but this can now be challenged in open court.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Black Friday sales officially start Friday, November 28, and run through Cyber Monday, November 30, 2026, and Lifehacker is sharing the best sales based on product reviews and comparisons before it's over.

It's Cyber Monday, and Lifehacker is sharing the best sales based on product reviews and comparisons before the sales are over.

Sales are accurate at the time of publication, but prices and inventory are always subject to change.

Not every Black Friday or Cyber Monday deal is as sweet as it seems. With electronics and tech in particular, you could be buying last year's model that has actually been on sale since the summer—and was maybe a better price a few months ago. Here’s how to avoid impulse buying a misleading Black Friday “deal” and make sure you’re getting the best bang for your buck.

When you see products like food, clothes, or home goods with a significant "Black Friday" or "Cyber Monday" tag slapped on them, it's probably safe to take advantage of that deal. Chances are it's the same exact product you'd find on other days of the year. The same can’t be noted for a TV, laptop, and other tech deals, where the product itself is constantly being upgraded.

According to recent reports, because tech is always evolving, and retailers want to move inventory before new models come out, electronics are especially susceptible to a practice known as "price anchoring." That's when retailers mark up prices in the weeks leading up to Black Friday, before "slashing" those prices back down, giving the appearance of a deal that isn't really a deal at all. Still, when you see that marked-up number, aka the "price anchor," you might get tricked into thinking you're saving money when you're not. There's also the false sense of urgency that gets created. It's second nature to assume that anything labeled "deal" won’t last long—even when this so-called deal price has actually been going on since the summer.

Sources indicate that price anchoring isn't even unique to Black Friday. The nonprofit Consumers’ Checkbook tracked prices at 25 major retailers over 33 weeks in 2022 and found that more than half the items tracked were offered at false discounts every week or almost every week. Less common, but also worth noting, is a known practice of "derivative" or retailer-exclusive models produced specifically for the holiday shopping season. These versions often feature cheaper components, fewer features, or lower specifications than their regular counterparts. A 55-inch TV from a reputable brand might look identical to the year-round model, but it could have a lower refresh rate, inferior panel technology, or fewer HDMI ports.

In the same vein, that "amazing deal" on a laptop might come with last year's processor, or a smartphone that's about to be replaced. The issue isn't that the tech is an older model, but again, it's that it probably has been at this low a price, or lower, since the summer. Alternatively, some deeply discounted electronics are refurbished units or open-box returns that have been repackaged. Again, while this isn't necessarily a bad thing, impulse buyers may not fully realize what they're buying.

In a recent development, the key phrasing here is impulse buying. Events like Black Friday are psychologically engineered to trigger impulse purchases. Limited-time offers, countdown clocks, and "while supplies last" warnings create artificial urgency. When you're caught up in the moment, it's easy to convince yourself you need a new tablet, smartwatch, or gaming console, even if you hadn't considered buying one before.

To avoid a low-key scam, do your research. The easiest way to tell that you’re getting the correct product is by checking the model or serial number. And with online shopping, finding and double-checking those numbers is quick and easy. In addition, don't just compare prices—compare specs. Look at processor speeds, RAM, storage capacity, screen resolution, refresh rates, and connectivity options. A $300 laptop isn't a deal if a slightly more expensive model offers significantly better performance that will last longer.

Industry observers note that if you do see a deal that catches your eye, it could pay to wait. Cyber Monday, post-Christmas sales, and even January clearances often feature electronics deals that rival or beat Black Friday prices, all without the famous chaos and pressure. Then again, you risk more “out-of-stock” results if you wait, so the risk is up to you, depending on the popularity of the item you’re eyeing (and how badly you want it).

The bottom line: Don’t fall victim to a falsely advertised lower-quality product, and do a little research to find actually good deals ahead of time.

Yes, Amazon has Black Friday sales, and we vet our deals to make sure they’re the best ones. You can also refer to guides like our live blog that have already done all of the vetting for you. And if you have an Amazon Prime membership, make the most of it.

Nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Black Friday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, November 30, 2026. The “best” sales depend on your needs, but in general, the biggest discounts tend to come from larger retailers who can afford lower prices: think places like Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and Home Depot. You can find all the best sales from major retailers on our Black Friday coverage.

According to recent reports, yes. Walmart, Best Buy, Target, and Home Depot will all have in-store deals, some of which you might not find online, so if you're able to take a trip to your local retailer, keep your eyes open for different deals.

Recent findings suggest that yes, Apple participates in Black Friday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

Industry observers note that black Friday sales officially begin Friday, November 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday,  November 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by December 2, 2026.

Andrea Scrosati is leaving Got Talent and Baywatch producer Fremantle after eight years to launch “a latest entrepreneurial venture.”.

Industry observers note that the exec will stay in his role as Fremantle Group COO and CEO of Continental Europe until the end of January 2027. Announcement of his exit comes three days after Deadline revealed Fremantle U.S. COO Suzanne Lopez was leaving after 23 years.

Scrosati can point to four Academy Awards and 17 Academy nominations, the Golden Lion at Venice and awards in Cannes and Berlin as an answer to Fremantle’s critics.

“Andrea has made an enormous contribution to Fremantle over the past eight years,” stated Fremantle CEO Jennifer Mullin. “He has been instrumental in our growth and transformation, from helping build Fremantle into a true portfolio company and leading our M&A strategy, to establishing our film strategy and constantly pushing us to think differently about innovation and the future of our business.

Industry observers note that “These eight years at Fremantle have been an extraordinary privilege,” added Scrosati. “Fremantle is a unique manufacturer, with incredible people, some of the world’s finest creative talent and an exceptional portfolio of IP. I leave with enormous pride in what we have achieved together and great affection for the company and everyone who makes it what it is. The time feels right for me to take the next step and focus on building something newly introduced.

How to Cancel Your Amazon Prime Membership After Black Friday and Cyber Monday

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (457 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Lifehacker

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • You can cancel your Prime subscription via web browser by first logging into your Amazon account.
  • Hover over the Accounts & Lists menu on the top-right of the window, then select the Prime Membership option.
  • Then tap the End Your Amazon Prime Membership button and finally click the Cancel Your Prime Membership orange button.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You can cancel your Prime subscription via web browser by first logging into your Amazon account. Amazon has a Cancel Your Prime Membership button on its support page to launch the process, or you can follow the steps detailed on Amazon's page:.

Head to Amazon.com in your web browser.

Hover over the Accounts & Lists menu on the top-right of the window, then select the Prime Membership option.

Then tap the End Your Amazon Prime Membership button and finally click the Cancel Your Prime Membership orange button.

Follow the on-screen instructions to cancel your Prime subscription.

Note that Amazon requires a bunch of clicks to finalize your cancellation, giving you lots of “opportunities” to change your mind.

Open the Amazon Shopping app on your mobile device.

Click the three horizontal lines on the bottom right.

Under Shop by Category, select Prime.

On the top bar, slide all the way to the end and select Help.

Then tap the End Your Amazon Prime Membership button and finally click the Cancel Your Prime Membership orange button.

Follow the on-screen instructions to cancel your Prime subscription.

As mentioned, closing your account will immediately end your access. Amazon also offers you the option to pause your benefits and billing temporarily instead of canceling them completely. Either way, your Amazon account is still active—you simply won’t have Prime benefits.

Finally, if you have other subscriptions connected to your Prime account, those will end when your billing is up. And if you signed up for Prime through the Android mobile shopping app or the Prime Video Android app, you’ll have to go through Google Subscription to manage your membership.

Industry observers note that yes, Amazon has Black Friday sales, and we vet our deals to make sure they’re the best ones. You can also refer to guides like our live blog that have already done all of the vetting for you. And if you have an Amazon Prime membership, make the most of it.

Industry observers note that nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Black Friday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, Nov. 30, 2026. The “best” sales depend on your needs, but in general, the biggest discounts tend to come from larger retailers who can afford lower prices: think places like Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and Home Depot. You can find all the best sales from major retailers on our Black Friday coverage.

In a recent development, yes. Walmart, Best Buy, Target, and Home Depot will all have in-store deals, some of which you might not find online, so if you're able to take a trip to your local retailer, keep your eyes open for different deals.

The last day to use the To Do apps is June 30, 2027. That date also applies to Windows, Android, and the web. The underlying service and sync support will retire later, according to Microsoft’s support document.

“Microsoft To Do is retiring,” Microsoft explains. “For work or school accounts, Microsoft Planner will be the destination for managing personal work tasks alongside assigned work. The updated My tasks experience begins rolling out in December 2026.”.

On the Mac, you can use Planner on the web or in Teams. Microsoft explicitly indicates it has no looks for a native Mac app.

Sources indicate that you can still see your existing To Do tasks in Planner through June 30, but your tasks and lists won’t carry over. Microsoft plans to offer an export option before the apps retire.

Sources indicate that planner doesn’t support personal Microsoft accounts however. If that’s how you use To Do, you’ll need to pick another task manager, even if you pay for Microsoft 365 Personal or Family, according to the company.

According to recent reports, the June shutdown will end a run of just over a decade for To Do on Apple platforms. Microsoft bought the company behind Wunderlist in 2015 and released the first iPhone preview of To Do in April 2017.

Microsoft has been trying to make Teams as the super app for some time now, as Planner is integrated into Teams. Teams is one of the prime examples of why super apps are terrible, with a bloated, web app-like experience.

Sources indicate that looking for a proper replacement? Apple’s built-in Reminders app can keep lists in sync between Apple devices, including a grocery list you share with family through iCloud.

If you liked To Do because it worked across platforms, Todoist has apps for iPhone, iPad, Mac, Windows, and Android.

#4457. Tech Report: The G1 Garbage Collector

Tech Report: The G1 Garbage Collector

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1472 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dev

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that the Garbage-First Garbage Collector (G1) is the default garbage collector on the JVM as of JDK 27, with JEP 523: Make G1 the Default Garbage Collector in All Environments, which made it the default in all environments.
  • Industry observers note that G1 was originally introduced in JDK 6u14 as an experimental feature, promoted to a standard feature in JDK 7u4, and designated the default garbage collector in JDK 9, taking over that role from ParallelGC.
  • At the time of its introduction, G1 was designed for server environments.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the Garbage-First Garbage Collector (G1) is the default garbage collector on the JVM as of JDK 27, with JEP 523: Make G1 the Default Garbage Collector in All Environments, which made it the default in all environments. It had been the default garbage collector in "server" environments since JDK 9, with JEP 248: Make G1 the Default Garbage Collector. G1 seeks to balance throughput and latency and is a good option for many workloads. In this article, we will cover a brief history of G1, its key design concepts, and how to use it.

Industry observers note that G1 was originally introduced in JDK 6u14 as an experimental feature, promoted to a standard feature in JDK 7u4, and designated the default garbage collector in JDK 9, taking over that role from ParallelGC. While G1 has taken over the role of default garbage collector from Parallel, it was originally introduced to replace the CMS (Concurrent-Mark-Sweep) Garbage Collector, which was deprecated in JDK 9 and removed in JDK 14.

At the time of its introduction, G1 was designed for server environments. Systems using G1 were expected to have multiple processors and large amounts of system memory (tens of GB) available. Continued development of G1 has reduced its system requirements, and now G1 can provide good performance even in resource constrained environments with only a single CPU and less than 2 GB of available system memory. This is why, as of JDK 27, it is the default garbage collector across all system configurations.

According to recent reports, in garbage collector design, the three primary design constraints are throughput, latency (pause time), and memory footprint. G1 seeks to maintain a balance between latency and throughput, rather than heavily optimizing for either. By comparison, ParallelGC primarily focuses on maximizing throughput, and ZGC focuses on minimizing latency. G1 also aims for more consistent pause times than the CMS collector it replaced.

In a recent development, as of the writing of this article, 12 JEPs relating to G1 have been delivered since JDK 8, with more changes planned for the future. Continued development has steadily improved G1's throughput, latency, and memory footprint.

G1 is a generational, incremental, parallel, mostly concurrent, stop-the-world, and evacuating garbage collector. For an explanation of each of these terms, check the Garbage Collection Concepts and JVM Collectors article on dev.java. This section covers some of the key design characteristics of G1.

Sources indicate that as mentioned in the previous section, G1 was originally designed with large "server-like" environments in mind. G1 is capable of efficiently marshalling the resources of systems with dozens of cores and addressing heaps measured in tens of GB.

Figure 03-01: Simplified representation of the G1 heap layout.

It has been revealed that G1 divides the heap into a set of regions (increments) of uniform size. Figure 03-01 is a simplified example of what the G1 heap space would look like. The size and number of regions, unless otherwise configured, are based on internal heuristics, with the overall heap size being the primary influence on both. These regions are then divided up into eden, survivor, old, and humongous regions.

Recent findings suggest that eden and survivor regions are both part of the "young" generation. On creation, an object is placed in an eden region. If that object survives a collection, it is evacuated (copied) into a survivor region. Unreachable objects are not deleted individually; rather, the region they are a part of is considered empty and is eligible for reuse by G1. Surviving objects, if they remain reachable, will be evacuated to a fresh survivor region on subsequent collections. If an object survives enough collections, based on internal heuristics unless otherwise configured, it will be evacuated to an old region, which is checked less frequently.

In a recent development, A humongous region is a contiguous space of one or more regions, reserved for a single "humongous" object. An object qualifies as "humongous" if it's larger than half the size of a single region. Humongous objects bypass the eden and survivor regions and are treated as equivalent to an old region by G1.

Figure 03-02: Simplified representation of the G1 garbage collection cycle.

The G1 garbage collection cycle (GC cycle) consists of both stop-the-world and concurrent behavior, both of which can run in parallel. Again, check Garbage Collection Concepts and JVM Collectors for definitions of these terms. Figure 03-02 is a simplified visualization of the G1 GC cycle and will help to contextualize this section.

In a recent development, at a high level, the G1 GC cycle consists of two phases: Young-Only and Space-Reclamation. G1 will start in the Young-Only phase, which, as the name suggests, means only young regions are collected. In G1, when a collection happens, the application is paused while G1 evacuates objects to upcoming regions or performs other GC work.

The concurrent behavior of G1 is primarily concerned with determining which objects in old regions are still active. The concurrent phase can be broken into three distinct parts and starts when old-generation occupancy reaches a threshold.

According to recent reports, concurrent Start is the first step in the concurrent phase and is a special pause. During this pause, normal evacuation of young regions still occurs, and G1 also initiates concurrent marking of old-generation regions to determine which objects are still reachable. It is also possible that G1 determines there is no need to follow through with marking, in which case a Concurrent Mark Undo pause occurs, and the Young-Only phase continues.

Sources indicate that remark is the second step in the concurrent phase. This is a special pause where no evacuation of young regions happens. Instead, during this pause, G1 finalizes concurrent marking and performs other work, such as reference processing, class unloading, and reclaiming empty regions. Between this phase and Cleanup, G1 will concurrently calculate information to be used during the Space-Reclamation phase.

Cleanup is the third and final step in the concurrent phase. This is also a special pause where no evacuation of young regions happens. During this pause, G1 determines if it should proceed to the Space-Reclamation phase. If a Space-Reclamation phase is determined to be necessary, the Young-Only phase will complete with a single Prepare Mixed young collection.

The Space-Reclamation phase consists of multiple mixed collections: collections where young and old regions are evacuated. G1 uses an efficiency algorithm to determine which old regions to collect first. A major factor in this algorithm is the amount of garbage in each old region, as regions with more garbage are more likely to yield large amounts of space. This is what "Garbage-First" in the G1 name refers to: it will reclaim the regions with the most garbage first.

The Space-Reclamation phase ends when G1 determines that evacuating more old regions is no longer worth the effort. At this point, G1 shifts back to the Young-Only phase.

For more technical details on G1, check the Garbage-First Garbage Collector guide and the G1 Stack Walker video at the bottom of this page.

G1 is explicitly enabled with the JVM argument -XX:+UseG1GC. If you are on JDK 27 or later, this argument is never necessary, as G1 was designated the default GC in all environments. From JDK 9 to JDK 26, G1 was chosen by the JVM if it detected two or more CPU cores and more than 1792 MB of available system memory; otherwise, SerialGC was used. If you are on JDK 8, you will need to explicitly set -XX:+UseG1GC to use G1, as ParallelGC is the default GC.

Generally speaking, owners should avoid applying too much configuration to garbage collectors. Often, "less is more," and the engineers who develop and maintain garbage collectors, G1 included, have worked toward having internal heuristics provide the best performance in most use cases "out of the box." As of the writing of this article, an upcoming change to G1, Automatic Heap Sizing, would handle one of the most important remaining aspects of G1 configuration: configuring the heap size.

In a recent development, when thinking about configuring a garbage collector, consider the three major constraints garbage collectors are designed around: throughput, latency, and memory footprint. G1 aims for a balance between latency and throughput. When a user provides custom configuration to G1, some tradeoff will be happening. A user increasing the heap size is trying to trade a larger memory footprint for reduced latency. A user setting a higher pause time goal for G1 will be trying to trade reduced latency for improved throughput. As a user considers configuring G1, there are no settings for simply "better" performance, but, at best, a tradeoff. Some configuration combinations simply lead to worse observed performance. Below are some key configuration parameters for G1.

For a deeper dive into configuring G1, check the guide maintained by the G1 engineering team.
